messages.title: Original request (undated, 'no rush'): three SDK jobs, host requirements, an account or a script
plain_english_bullets: The sender is Jeremy's Claude (an AI assistant writing for Jeremy, the SDK-side engineer). The message is addressed to Jibin. It says there is no rush.

Jeremy's team wants to run SDK tests on phoenix-crb. SDK means Positron's software development kit: the runtime, compiler and test tools, staged on the host at ~/positron/src/phoenix-int. phoenix-crb is the Arm server at 192.168.2.45 (Linux hostname 'ubuntu', firmware name 'Phoenix Reference Server').

The tests use only the host CPU. No Asimov card (Positron's accelerator board) needs to be attached. None is attached today [phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section devices: the line '--- lspci positron/accelerator match' is followed by nothing].
They will run one job at a time. This is a promise about load, not a request for a host-side lock.

Job 1 is a timing test. The runtime drives a fake device (the SDK's null_timing backend: a device thread posts each pass's completion at a modelled time and computes nothing). The test measures the time the host software adds to each step (one forward pass of the model), to the gaps between tokens, to time to first token (TTFT) and to waking a waiting reader (a thread that sleeps until a result is posted).
Job 2 is the SDK's sampling unit tests (tests of the code that picks the next token from model outputs), built and run natively on Arm (aarch64, the host's architecture).
Job 3 is a timed compile of a small model. The SDK's gate list names this 'compile-0.8b', the wall time of the Qwen3.5-0.8B compile [tools/conformance/README.md line 16, read on the host 2026-10-22].

Host need 1: at least one core, better two, isolated with isolcpus (a kernel boot parameter that removes CPUs from the scheduler's load balancing) and nohz_full (a kernel feature that stops the periodic timer tick on a CPU that runs one task), ideally with rcu_nocbs (a boot parameter that moves RCU callback work, kernel bookkeeping, off those CPUs), and with IRQs (hardware interrupts) kept off them. The other cores stay with the OS and the SDK's worker threads.

Host need 2: a fixed CPU clock, meaning the performance cpufreq governor (the kernel policy that always requests the highest clock) and no boost (no clock above the nominal maximum), if the board allows it.
Host need 3: nothing else running during a timed run. A nightly window (a reserved period at night) is acceptable.

Host need 4: clang 18 (a C and C++ compiler), CMake 3.25 or newer (a build configurator), Ninja (a build runner) and Python 3.11 or newer with development headers. Jeremy says Ubuntu 24.04's packages cover these.
Host need 5: about 100 GB of disk. The account needs no sudo (administrator rights) and no outbound network. Jeremy says his side copies everything in.

Ask A: a local account named positron-perf with SSH key login (login by cryptographic key, no password), reachable from Jeremy's laptop directly or through sw-dev-01 (the SDK team's development host; DNS on Jibin's workstation gives it the LAN address 192.168.2.39 and the Tailscale address 100.124.2.53).
Ask B, the alternative: if Jibin would rather not hand out an account, Jibin runs a script that Jeremy sends.

asks.ask: Run SDK tests on phoenix-crb, host CPU only, no Asimov card attached
asks.status_evidence: A job has already run under the account: phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section churn_r1_job_log: '== 2026-10-21T18:32:09Z host=ubuntu head=ead1e9ab...' and '== label rc=3 (168 s)'. No accelerator is attached: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section devices, '--- lspci positron/accelerator match' prints nothing.

asks.ask: One job at a time (implicit serialization rule)
asks.status_evidence: No host-side mechanism enforces it: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section background: 'LSF_ENVDIR=unset', 'lsfd=inactive', 'docker ... No such file or directory'. The SDK's perf lane holds a lock while its job runs: phoenix-crb-round5.txt, section 'perf_lane.py header': '3. takes the lane's lock and starts one detached job that holds it (tools/perf/perf_job.sh)'. Jeremy's churn job script has no lock: phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section runs_and_checks, ev3-churn-job.sh runs 'taskset -c 120-127 prlimit ... bash tools/ci/run_scheduled_gate.sh churn' directly. Serialization today is by convention only.
asks.why_jeremy: He must say whether every job on his side goes through a lane lock, or whether Jibin should add a host-side reservation rule (a calendar or a lock file). The host has two other users: arm on the tty1 console and the machine 'alpha' at 192.168.1.200 (section logins).

asks.ask: Job 1: the timing test on the fake device (per-step overhead, inter-token gaps, TTFT, reader wake-up)
asks.status_evidence: One run exists and produced no valid measurement: phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section rejudge_summary: 'verdict = "INFRA"', 'problems = ["the fake device's lateness voids the record", ...]'. The void criterion is the MEAN lateness: docs/null-timing.md line 87 (read on the host 2026-10-22): '`void`, true when the mean lateness passes the band'; backends/null_timing/record.h line 45: 'a run whose mean lateness passes this share of the cohort period is void'. The numbers: phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section runs_and_checks, r1-run.rec_bind.check.txt: 'late_mean_s': 6.246e-06, 'late_max_s': 0.000220151, 'lateness_band_s': 2.502e-06, 'void': True (mean 6.2 us against a 2.5 us band, 2.5 times over; maximum 220 us). The device thread is not pinned: a grep of backends/ for setaffinity, pthread_setaffinity, sched_setscheduler and leave_pass_cpu returned nothing (host 2026-10-22). It runs among CPUs 120-126, which sat at the minimum clock for the whole run: ~/positron/runs/churn-r1/isol.samples.jsonl (34 samples over 168 s, read on the host 2026-10-22) shows cpu124 and cpu125 at 1,600,000 kHz in 34 of 34 samples, cpu120 and cpu126 in 33 of 34, cpu121 and cpu123 in 31 of 34, cpu122 in 29 of 34, while cpu127 (the pass core) was at 2,800,000 kHz in 26 of 34. Hypothesis, not proven: the 1.6 GHz clock on the device thread's CPU causes the lateness; the measurement is a re-run of ~/positron/runs/ev3-churn-job.sh after the performance governor is set, reading late_mean_s.
asks.why_jeremy: Where the fake device thread runs and whether to pin it is harness code on his side. He should also say whether a run with the performance governor alone (before the reboot) would count, so the governor effect can be separated from the isolcpus effect.

asks.ask: Job 2: the sampling unit tests, natively on Arm
asks.status_evidence: No test run is recorded on the host. The three build logs under ~/positron/runs/build-*/build.log contain no ctest or pytest output; 'sampling' matches only compile lines such as '[14/334] Building CXX object runtime/sampling/CMakeFiles/positron_rt_sampling.dir/contract_exp.cpp.o' (host grep 2026-10-22). The build job built only three targets: phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section runs_and_checks, ev2-build-job.sh: '--target _positron_core positron-harness positron-cpuref'. No file named *ctest*, *pytest*, LastTest.log or *unit* exists under ~/positron/runs, ~/positron/work or ~/positron/check (host find 2026-10-22). A ctest or pytest log, or Jeremy's word, would decide it.
asks.why_jeremy: He must say whether these tests were run (perhaps interactively, without a log) and whether they need a scheduled slot.

asks.ask: Job 3: a timed compile of a small model
asks.status_evidence: The SDK's gate list says the compile-timing gate is not run yet: tools/conformance/README.md line 16 (host 2026-10-22): 'compile-0.8b | wall time of the Qwen3.5-0.8B compile, against a budget registered after the first measuring runs; registered uncalibrated | the perf lane, on the perf host (spec §12.2), which does not run it yet; no hosted runner or shared LSF worker times it'. The churn job did build the 0.8B fixture (phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section fixture_dense_log: 'P-TP1, S=4, max_context_tokens=2048; 128 fragments') and priced its table ('priced in 2.7 s', ~/positron/runs/churn-r1/record/table-dense.log, host 2026-10-22), but no file records a compile wall time as a result.
asks.why_jeremy: He must say which compile counts and when it runs. If it is the compile-0.8b gate of the perf lane, the perf lane's host rule (isolcpus plus nohz_full) applies.

asks.ask: At least one core (two better) isolated with isolcpus
asks.status_evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpu_summary: 'isolated: ' (empty). Section identity: 'cmdline: BOOT_IMAGE=/vmlinuz-7.1.3-arm-agi-... root=UUID=... ro console=tty1 console=ttyAMA0' (no isolcpus). The running kernel supports it: section kernel_config 'CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION=y'. It is a boot parameter, so root must edit GRUB and reboot: section boot_and_kernels: '/boot/grub/grub.cfg: Permission denied' for the account, and the drop-in '/etc/default/grub.d/50-cloudimg-settings.cfg' sets 'GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="console=tty1 console=ttyAMA0"', so a new drop-in that sets GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX plus update-grub is the clean route. Kernel docs (kernel.org admin-guide/kernel-parameters, isolcpus= 'domain', read 2026-10-22): a CPU isolated this way cannot be returned to the scheduling domains at runtime; cpusets are recommended for dynamic setups.
asks.why_jeremy: Message 1 asks for one or two cores, message 2 for one, message 3 for cores 120-127 (eight). His churn job pins the pass thread to CPU 127 and lets five other threads float over 120-126 (isol.samples.jsonl, host 2026-10-22: 'positron-harnes' seen on every CPU 120 to 126, 'positron-scrub' on 123, 124 and 126, allowed mask '120-126'). On isolcpus CPUs the scheduler does no load balancing, so those threads would stop moving. He must choose: isolate only the pass core(s), or all eight and pin each thread.

asks.ask: nohz_full on the isolated cores
asks.status_evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section kernel_config: '# CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL is not set'. Section cpu_summary: 'nohz_full: cat: /sys/devices/system/cpu/nohz_full: No such file or directory'; that sysfs file exists only under CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL (torvalds master drivers/base/cpu.c: nohz_full_show() and its attribute entry are inside '#ifdef CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL', read 2026-10-22). On such a kernel the boot parameter is parsed and then dropped: torvalds master kernel/sched/isolation.c, housekeeping_setup(): 'if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL))' then 'pr_warn("Housekeeping: nohz unsupported." " Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL\n")' and 'return 0'. Measured tick today: phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section residual_tick_under_load: 'busy 5 s: arch_timer=1261 IPIs=1 all_irqs=1264 (HZ=250 would give 1250 ticks in 5 s)', one timer interrupt every 4 ms on a busy CPU. A kernel with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL=y is needed. The installed stock kernel has it ('/boot/config-6.8.0-147-generic: CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL=y', section kernel_config) but has never booted on this board (section logins: all five 'system boot' lines say '7.1.3-arm-agi-20'), and the vendor kernel carries silicon workarounds (phoenix-crb-followup.txt, section dmesg_greps: 'GICv3: Arm AGI CPU A0 detected, enabling GIC erratum workaround', 'CPU features: detected: Broken broadcast TLBI completion'). The vendor kernel source is not on the host: /usr/src/linux-headers-7.1.3-arm-agi-... holds only 'Makefile Module.symvers arch include scripts', no kernel/ directory, 36 .c files (host 2026-10-22). Secure Boot is off (efivar SecureBoot data byte 0, host 2026-10-22), so a locally built kernel needs no signature.
asks.why_jeremy: He must say whether the counted numbers need nohz_full before 5 Nov. tools/perf refuses a host without it (phoenix-crb-round5.txt, records.py: 'no online core is in both isolcpus and nohz_full (§12.2 l.2049)'); the latency judge does not check it (latency_judge.py isolated(), lines 1166-1169 on the host 2026-10-22, only requires pass_thread_core to be an integer). Message 2 already allows 'the rest of the list' to follow later.

asks.ask: rcu_nocbs on the isolated cores (ideally)
asks.status_evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section kernel_config: '# CONFIG_RCU_EXPERT is not set' and no CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU line at all (the grep pattern in inspect.sh line 29 includes RCU_NOCB). torvalds master kernel/rcu/Kconfig (read 2026-10-22): RCU_NOCB_CPU 'depends on TREE_RCU' and 'depends on RCU_EXPERT || NO_HZ_FULL', so the option does not exist on this kernel and rcu_nocbs= would be an unknown parameter. kernel/time/Kconfig: NO_HZ_FULL 'select RCU_NOCB_CPU', and the kernel-parameters doc says nohz_full CPUs get 'their RCU callbacks offloaded' automatically. So this ask is covered by the nohz_full ask.

asks.ask: IRQs kept off the isolated cores
asks.status_evidence: Today only the per-CPU NVMe queue interrupts reach CPUs 120-127: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section interrupts: 'TOTAL irq dirs parsed: 452 with effective affinity touching 120-127: 16', all named nvme0q119-126 and nvme1q119-126, one per CPU (for example '311 127 affinity_hint,nvme0q126,'). The 64 network queues sit on CPUs 0-63 and 196 other IRQs have effective affinity CPU 0. Nothing enforces this: 'default_smp_affinity: ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff' (all 128 CPUs). Timer and IPIs still land there: '12 total=23272572 on120_127=5327444 GICv3 26 Level arch_timer' and 'IPI1 total=3505125 on120_127=123695 Function call interrupts' since boot. The NVMe queues cannot be moved: they are managed interrupts, and the kernel-parameters doc (isolcpus= managed_irq, read 2026-10-22) says their affinity 'cannot be changed via the /proc/irq/* interfaces', that when 'a queue's affinity mask contains only isolated CPUs then this parameter has no effect on the interrupt routing decision', and that such interrupts 'are only delivered when tasks running on those isolated CPUs submit IO'. Movable IRQs can be set live by root: /proc/irq/default_smp_affinity is '-rw-r--r-- 1 root root' (host 2026-10-22); the irqaffinity= boot parameter only makes that persistent. The tick and IPIs need nohz_full, a kernel change.

asks.ask: Fixed clock: performance cpufreq governor
asks.status_evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpufreq: 'governors: 128 schedutil;', 'avail governors: ondemand userspace performance schedutil', 'drivers: 128 cppc_cpufreq;', 'related/affected 120: 120 / 120' (each CPU is its own policy), 'perms: ... -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 4096 Oct 21 18:31 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy120/scaling_governor' (policy0 and policy127 are the same mode, host 2026-10-22). Root can write 'performance' live; no reboot. A live write does not survive a reboot: section kernel_config 'CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_DEFAULT_GOV_SCHEDUTIL=y', so persistence needs 'cpufreq.default_governor=performance' on the kernel command line or a boot-time unit. Why it matters: under schedutil a sleep-then-spin thread stays at the minimum clock (phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section freq_files: 'freq.sleep.txt: 89 1600000 1 1711718'), and during churn-r1 CPUs 120-126 were at 1,600,000 kHz in 29 to 34 of 34 samples while CPU 127 was at 2,800,000 kHz in 26 of 34 (isol.samples.jsonl, host 2026-10-22). A busy CPU does reach the top clock: phoenix-crb-followup.txt, section cpufreq_extra: 'delivered perf = 139.8 units -> est. 2796 MHz' over a 3.01 s pinned spin. Scope: under churn the run's other threads and the fake device thread use CPUs 120-126, under the perf lane they use CPUs 0-119 (phoenix-crb-round5.txt, records.py choose_cores: housekeeping cores plus one isolated core), so host-wide performance is the one setting that fits both.
asks.why_jeremy: Not needed to apply it. The acceptance rule for 'fixed' (what spread of delivered MHz over a full run) is a separate question for him; the account can measure the delivered clock without root from acpi_cppc/feedback_ctrs (mode 0444, phoenix-crb-followup.txt, section cpufreq_extra).

asks.ask: Fixed clock: no boost
asks.status_evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpufreq: 'global boost: 0', 'policy120 boost: 0', 'highest_perf=140', 'nominal_perf=140', 'nominal_freq=2800' (highest equals nominal, so no clock above 2.8 GHz exists on this firmware). Section cpu_summary: 'Frequency boost: disabled'.

asks.ask: Nothing else running during a timed run; a nightly window is fine
asks.status_evidence: The host is near idle: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpu_activity: 'cpu120 idle=100.0%' through 'cpu127 idle=100.0%' over 5 s; section identity: 'load average: 0.00, 0.00, 0.00'. During churn-r1 the rest of the host was idle: phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section churn_r1_job_log: '"busy_share_cpus_0_119": 0.0002'. Periodic work remains: section background: running services include 'netperf.service', 'unattended-upgrades.service', 'cron.service', 'smartmontools.service'; phoenix-crb-followup.txt, section services_detail: apt timers 'OnCalendar=*-*-* 6,18:00' with 'RandomizedDelaySec=12h' (so apt-daily can fire at any hour; last run 'Wed 2026-10-21 21:57:44 UTC'), sysstat from both the timer 'OnCalendar=*:00/10' and cron '5-55/10 * * * * root ... debian-sa1 1 1', fstrim next 'Mon 2026-10-26 00:27:20 UTC', logrotate and dpkg-db-backup at '00:00:00 UTC'. Other users: section logins 'arm tty1 Oct 20 19:31' (console session still open) and arm sessions from 192.168.1.200 ('alpha.positron.internal' per DNS on Jibin's workstation) of 2 to 4 h on 20-21 Oct. The SDK's own quiet rule is narrower than 'nothing running': tools/perf/host_facts.sh (host 2026-10-22) flags other users' processes at '$4 + 0 >= 5.0' percent CPU and a CI runner process, and records.py has 'LOAD_MAX = 0.5' for the one-minute load. Pausing timers and services needs root; no reboot.
asks.why_jeremy: He must give the run windows with a timezone. The host runs UTC (section identity 'Time zone: Etc/UTC'), Jibin is at UTC-7 (PDT), Jeremy at UTC-4 (EDT, from his commit's '-0400' in phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section git_state); after 2026-11-01 the US offsets become UTC-8 and UTC-5.

asks.ask: clang 18, CMake 3.25 or newer, Ninja, Python 3.11 or newer with dev headers
asks.status_evidence: Met at user level by the SDK side: phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section toolchain_readme: '~/positron/toolchains/sdk-ci-2026-10/ | conda-forge environment: gcc/g++ 13.3.0, clang/clang++ 18.1.8, CMake 3.31.6, Ninja 1.13.2' and 'venv on /usr/bin/python3.12 (3.12.3)'; '--- toolchain env binaries': 'clang: clang version 18.1.8', 'ninja: 1.13.2', 'cmake: cmake version 3.31.6'. phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section tools: 'Python 3.12.3', 'Python.h=/usr/include/python3.12/Python.h', 'libpython3.12-dev:arm64 3.12.3-1ubuntu0.17'. System-wide: 'clang-18 not in PATH', 'ninja not in PATH', 'cmake version 3.28.3'. No root action is required. The README's 'approved by Jeremy that day' is the SDK side's own note, not evidence from Jeremy.

asks.ask: About 100 GB of disk
asks.status_evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section storage: '/dev/nvme0n1p1 ext4 1.7T 41G 1.7T 3% /' (/home is on it; 1.7 TB free), 'home usage: 7.7G', 'quota: ... No such file or directory' (no quota tool, so no limit).

asks.ask: No sudo for the account (a statement of need, not a request to act)
asks.status_evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section network_access: '--- sudo: sudo: a password is required', 'sudo -l: sudo: a password is required', 'groups: positron-perf users'; section logins: 'sudo:x:27:arm' (only arm is in the sudo group). phoenix-crb-followup.txt, section services_detail: 'positron-perf L 2026-10-21 0 99999 7 -1' (password locked); '/etc/sudoers.d/positron-perf-setup' is 49 bytes, mode '-r--r----- 1 root root', and reading it gives 'Permission denied' (host 2026-10-22), so its content is unknown. Related limit: real-time scheduling is refused ('chrt -f 1 test: chrt: failed to set pid 0's policy: Operation not permitted', 'rtprio hard limit: 0', section perf_rt_checks). The runtime does not use SCHED_FIFO today (phoenix-crb-round5.txt, section 'runtime C++: scheduling policy / affinity / mlock use' lists only sched_setaffinity and pthread_setaffinity_np), but the design spec mentions SCHED_FIFO for the interpreter core (section 'docs: isolation / governor / nohz mentions', design-12-repository.md line 182).

asks.ask: No outbound network needed ('we copy everything in'; a statement of need)
asks.status_evidence: No action is needed: the host has outbound internet (phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section network_access: 'https pypi: 200', 'https ubuntu archive: 200', 'tcp 140.82.112.3:443 (github ip) reachable'). The SDK side's staging used it: phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section src_work_venvs, work/venv-setup/pip-install.log: 'Downloading numpy-2.5.3-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_27_aarch64...whl (15.7 MB)' at '44.8 MB/s'; work/toolchain-setup/create.log: 'Using Cached Shard Index for conda-forge/linux-aarch64'. If outbound were blocked to match the sentence, re-creating the toolchain from the lockfile would fail.

asks.ask: Local account positron-perf with SSH key login, reachable from Jeremy's laptop directly or through sw-dev-01
asks.status_evidence: Account: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section identity: 'uid=1001(positron-perf) gid=1001(positron-perf) groups=1001(positron-perf),100(users)'. Keys: phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section authorized_key_fingerprints: 'jeremy@sw-dev-01 (ED25519)', 'jeremy@DESKTOP-V2B1166 (ED25519)' and Jibin's 'positron-perf@phoenix (ED25519)'; the file's mtime is 16:53 UTC on 21 Oct (section network_access), written during positron-perf sessions from 192.168.2.136 (Jibin's workstation claude-agentsrv) at 16:52-16:53 UTC. Logins by the SDK side happened: the system journal, read as the account on 2026-10-22, shows 'sshd[7790]: Disconnected from user positron-perf 192.168.2.39 port 46146' at 17:07:35 UTC and three more sessions from 192.168.2.39 at 18:22, 18:23 and 18:27 UTC, plus about 50 sessions from 192.168.1.200 between 17:07 and 18:32 UTC, for example 'sshd[8158]: Disconnected from user positron-perf 192.168.1.200 port 55041' at 18:11:12 UTC, the minute ~/positron was created (phoenix-crb-followup.txt, section home_positron). DNS on Jibin's workstation (search domains porgy-gecko.ts.net and positron.internal) resolves 192.168.2.39 to 'sw-dev-01.positron.internal' (and sw-dev-01 also to the Tailscale address 100.124.2.53) and 192.168.1.200 to 'alpha.positron.internal'. So the sw-dev-01 path works (draft gap G2 closed). Which key each session used is not visible to the account (sshd's 'Accepted publickey' lines are root-only; the grep returned none), and who operates 'alpha' is unknown (draft gap G6 half closed).
asks.why_jeremy: Only to confirm that his laptop path (the DESKTOP-V2B1166 key) also works and to say which machine 'alpha' (192.168.1.200) is. Nothing blocks on it.

asks.ask: Alternative: Jibin runs a script that Jeremy sends
asks.status_evidence: Superseded: the account exists and has been used (phoenix-crb-followup.txt, section home_positron: ~/positron, 7.7 GB, created 2026-10-21 18:11 to 18:57 UTC; phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section churn_r1_job_log: a job ran at 18:32 UTC). No action is needed.

messages.title: Follow-up (undated): account and one isolated core by Friday 2026-10-23, counted runs from Monday 2026-10-26, for the 5 November demo
plain_english_bullets: The sender is again Jeremy's Claude. It thanks Jibin and gives 'one update since this morning'. Which message that morning refers to is not stated, so the order of messages 2 and 3 is uncertain [requests.txt header: 'Order as supplied: original (undated, no rush), follow-up (dated deadline), latest (21 Oct 2026 morning)'].

There is now a date. The per-user latency runs (runs graded by the SDK's latency judge, tools/conformance/latency_judge.py, against the gate 'per-user-latency.qwen3_5_0_8b.P-TP1') for the 5 November demo need a quiet host.

The shared LSF workers are too noisy for those runs. LSF is IBM's batch job scheduler; the SDK's dev lane submits jobs to it from sw-dev-01. This host runs no LSF [phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section background: 'LSF_ENVDIR=unset', 'lsfd=inactive'].
Deadline 1: the positron-perf account and one isolated core should be ready by Friday 2026-10-23.

Deadline 2: counted runs should start Monday 2026-10-26. 'Counted' matches the SDK's rule that timings count only from the perf host, and phoenix-crb is that host [tools/conformance/README.md line 225, read on the host 2026-10-22: 'the lane's timings count only from the perf host'].
The rest of message 1's list can follow later. This already permits a Friday setup without nohz_full and rcu_nocbs.

If any step is a problem, for example the reboot that isolcpus needs, Jeremy wants to be told, and the two sides will agree a workaround. This is an implicit request for a status reply, not a pre-approval of any particular workaround.

asks.ask: positron-perf account ready by Friday 2026-10-23
asks.status_evidence: Same evidence as message 1's account ask: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section identity 'uid=1001(positron-perf)'; three authorized keys (phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section authorized_key_fingerprints); sessions from sw-dev-01 (192.168.2.39) and alpha (192.168.1.200) on 2026-10-21 (system journal, host 2026-10-22); 7.7 GB staged (phoenix-crb-followup.txt, section home_positron); a job ran at 18:32 UTC (phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section churn_r1_job_log).

asks.ask: One isolated core ready by Friday 2026-10-23
asks.status_evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpu_summary: 'isolated: ' (empty). Jeremy's own snapshot at job time agrees: phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section isol_before_summary: 'isolated: ""', 'nohz_full: "(no file)"', 'governors: {"schedutil": "128 cpus"}'; section rejudge_summary: '"core_isolated": false, ... "isolated_cpus": []'. Two routes. (a) isolcpus on the kernel command line: root plus one reboot on the current kernel ('CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION=y', section kernel_config). (b) A cgroup v2 cpuset 'isolated' partition: root, no reboot, but the cpuset controller is not enabled below the root ('subtree_control: cpu memory pids', section cgroups; the file is '-rw-r--r-- 1 root root', host 2026-10-22), the job's processes must be placed in that cgroup by root, nothing persists across a reboot, and /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated stays empty, because torvalds master drivers/base/cpu.c print_cpus_isolated() (read 2026-10-22) prints the complement of 'housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT)', the boot-time set only. So churn.py would record core_isolated=false (phoenix-crb-round5.txt, placement(): 'isolated = sorted(_cpus(CPU_SYSFS / "isolated"))', '"core_isolated": core in isolated'), and so would demo_d17.py (lines 1366-1380, host 2026-10-22).
asks.why_jeremy: He must accept isolcpus without nohz_full for Friday (message 2 allows the rest later), name the core(s), and, if the reboot cannot happen by Friday, say whether route (b) with core_isolated=false is acceptable. The latency judge itself does not require core_isolated=true: latency_judge.py isolated() (lines 1166-1169, host 2026-10-22) returns true whenever pass_thread_core is an integer.

messages.title: Latest request, 21 October 2026 (morning): isolate cores 120-127 and set the performance governor
plain_english_bullets: Jeremy wants Phoenix (phoenix-crb) usable for the SDK's latency runs.

He asks for a few isolated cores for the runtime's pass thread. The pass thread is the one thread per runtime, named 'positron-pass', that plans and binds each forward pass; the SDK pins it to one core [phoenix-crb-round5.txt, section 'docs: isolation / governor / nohz mentions', docs/runtime-v2.md line 304].
His example is isolcpus, nohz_full and rcu_nocbs on cores 120-127. That is eight cores; messages 1 and 2 asked for one or two.
He asks for the performance cpufreq governor so the clock stays fixed.
He states that both changes need root and a reboot. That is wrong for the governor and incomplete for nohz_full and rcu_nocbs (see corrections).

He states that today the governor is schedutil (the policy that scales the clock with load) and no cores are isolated. That is accurate [phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpufreq: 'governors: 128 schedutil;'; section cpu_summary: 'isolated: ' empty].
The phrase 'whenever you have a moment' signals no hard deadline. It conflicts with message 2's Friday deadline unless message 2 was written after this one.

asks.ask: isolcpus on cores 120-127
asks.status_evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpu_summary: 'isolated: ' (empty); section kernel_config: 'CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION=y'. GRUB keeps the vendor kernel as the default entry (section boot_and_kernels: 'GRUB_DEFAULT=saved', 'saved_entry=Advanced options for Ubuntu>Ubuntu, with Linux 7.1.3-arm-agi-...'). CPUs 120-127 are eight separate cores with no SMT siblings (section topology_120_127: 'cpu127 ... siblings=127'). Jeremy's job already uses exactly these CPUs: phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section runs_and_checks, ev3-churn-job.sh: 'taskset -c 120-127 ... run_scheduled_gate.sh churn', with 'pass_thread_core': 127 and 'run_cpus': [120..126] (phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section rejudge_summary). Command-line warning: the 'nohz' flag of isolcpus must not be used on this kernel, because torvalds master kernel/sched/isolation.c housekeeping_isolcpus_setup() maps 'nohz,' to the same flag as nohz_full and housekeeping_setup() then drops the whole isolcpus parameter ('return 0' after 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported'; read 2026-10-22). The 'domain' flag also removes the CPUs from unbound workqueues: torvalds master kernel/workqueue.c workqueue_init_early(): 'restrict_unbound_cpumask("HK_TYPE_DOMAIN", housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN))'.
asks.why_jeremy: Isolating all eight removes load balancing among them. In churn-r1 his harness threads moved across all of 120-126 (isol.samples.jsonl, host 2026-10-22: 'positron-harnes' sampled on CPUs 120, 121, 122, 123, 124, 125 and 126; 'positron-scrub' on 123, 124 and 126; allowed mask '120-126'), and churn.py sets that mask for them (phoenix-crb-round5.txt, placement() body: 'os.sched_setaffinity(0, cpus)'). The perf lane instead puts workers on non-isolated cores (records.py choose_cores: housekeeping cores plus the first isolated nohz_full core). He must choose: isolate only the pass core(s), which fits churn's taskset, or all eight, which fits the perf lane, and then pin each thread.

asks.ask: nohz_full on cores 120-127
asks.status_evidence: Same evidence as message 1's nohz_full ask: '# CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL is not set' (phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section kernel_config), '/sys/devices/system/cpu/nohz_full: No such file or directory' (section cpu_summary), and the parameter is dropped at boot on such a kernel (torvalds master kernel/sched/isolation.c, 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported. Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL'). A kernel with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL=y is needed: a rebuilt vendor kernel (source not on the host; it was built by 'avadnaik@2paltra-216' with 'gcc-14 (Ubuntu 14.3.0-12ubuntu1~24~ppa1)', phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section boot_and_kernels, uname version string) or the stock 6.8.0-147-generic, which has never booted on this board.
asks.why_jeremy: Whether the counted runs can wait for a rebuilt kernel or proceed without nohz_full (accepting the 250 Hz tick on busy isolated cores).

asks.ask: rcu_nocbs on cores 120-127
asks.status_evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section kernel_config: no CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU line and '# CONFIG_RCU_EXPERT is not set'. torvalds master kernel/rcu/Kconfig: RCU_NOCB_CPU 'depends on RCU_EXPERT || NO_HZ_FULL'. A NO_HZ_FULL kernel brings it automatically (kernel/time/Kconfig: NO_HZ_FULL 'select RCU_NOCB_CPU').

asks.ask: performance cpufreq governor so the clock stays fixed
asks.status_evidence: Same evidence as message 1's governor ask: 'governors: 128 schedutil;', 'avail governors: ondemand userspace performance schedutil', scaling_governor is '-rw-r--r-- 1 root root' (phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpufreq); root writes it live, no reboot, no kernel change; persistence needs 'cpufreq.default_governor=performance' or a boot unit because 'CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_DEFAULT_GOV_SCHEDUTIL=y' (section kernel_config). The governor only requests the highest clock; the delivered clock over a full run is unmeasured (only a 3.01 s spin: 'delivered perf = 139.8 units -> est. 2796 MHz', phoenix-crb-followup.txt, section cpufreq_extra). No thermal zone exists ('thermal_zone*: ... No such file or directory', section cpufreq), so throttling cannot be read from sysfs; acpi_cppc/feedback_ctrs (mode 0444) give the delivered clock to any user.

asks.ask: 'whenever you have a moment': confirm whether the Friday 2026-10-23 deadline of message 2 still stands
asks.status_evidence: Insufficient data. requests.txt gives only the supplied order ('original, follow-up, latest'); message 2's 'one update since this morning' may refer to message 3 (dated '21 October 2026 (morning)') or to message 1. Only Jeremy can say.
asks.why_jeremy: He must confirm which message is the latest and whether Friday 2026-10-23 still holds.

corrections_to_jeremys_statements: Message 3, 'Both need root and a reboot': wrong in both directions. The governor needs root but no reboot: scaling_governor is a live sysfs file owned by root ('-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 4096 Oct 21 18:31 /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy120/scaling_governor') and 'performance' is in 'avail governors: ondemand userspace performance schedutil' [phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpufreq; policy0 and policy127 have the same mode, host check 2026-10-22]. nohz_full and rcu_nocbs (also asked in message 1) need more than a reboot: the running kernel has '# CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL is not set' and no CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU line [section kernel_config], and '/sys/devices/system/cpu/nohz_full: No such file or directory' [section cpu_summary]. On such a kernel the nohz_full= parameter is rejected with 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported. Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL' and dropped (torvalds master kernel/sched/isolation.c, housekeeping_setup(), read 2026-10-22), and rcu_nocbs= is an unknown parameter because RCU_NOCB_CPU 'depends on RCU_EXPERT || NO_HZ_FULL' (kernel/rcu/Kconfig). Only isolcpus is 'root plus reboot' on this kernel.

Message 1, 'No sudo and no outbound network; we copy everything in': the second half was not followed. The host has outbound access ('https pypi: 200', 'https ubuntu archive: 200', 'dns github.com: 20.29.134.23' [phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section network_access]) and the SDK side's staging downloaded on the host: work/venv-setup/pip-install.log has 23 'Downloading' lines, for example 'Downloading numpy-2.5.3-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_27_aarch64.manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl (15.7 MB)' at '44.8 MB/s', and work/toolchain-setup/create.log shows micromamba fetching from conda-forge ('Using Cached Shard Index for conda-forge/linux-aarch64') [phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section src_work_venvs]. If outbound had been blocked to match the sentence, that setup would have failed. The 'no sudo' half is accurate.

Message 3, 'a few isolated cores for the runtime's pass thread': the pass thread is not what voided the first run, so cores for it alone do not address the current blocker. churn-r1 was voided because the fake device thread's MEAN lateness (6.2 us) exceeded the band (2.5 us): 'late_mean_s': 6.246e-06 ... 'lateness_band_s': 2.502e-06, 'void': True [phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section runs_and_checks, r1-run.rec_bind.check.txt]; the rule is on the mean: docs/null-timing.md line 87 '`void`, true when the mean lateness passes the band' and backends/null_timing/record.h line 45 (host 2026-10-22). The device thread is not pinned (grep of backends/ for setaffinity, pthread_setaffinity, sched_setscheduler and leave_pass_cpu returned nothing; the only pinning code is pass_loop.cpp and worker_thread.cpp [phoenix-crb-round5.txt, section 'runtime C++: scheduling policy / affinity / mlock use']). It runs among CPUs 120-126, which stayed at 1,600,000 kHz in 29 to 34 of 34 samples during the run while the pass core 127 was at 2,800,000 kHz in 26 of 34 (isol.samples.jsonl, host 2026-10-22). The performance governor on the device thread's CPUs is the first-order fix to test; isolation of the pass core is a second step.

Messages 1, 2 and 3 disagree on how many cores: 'at least one core (two would be better)' (message 1), 'one isolated core' (message 2), 'cores 120-127', eight cores (message 3). Not a factual error, but a decision is needed: his own job used all eight ('taskset -c 120-127', pass thread on 127, other threads on 120-126 [phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section runs_and_checks; phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section rejudge_summary]), and those other threads migrated across all of 120-126 during the run (isol.samples.jsonl, host 2026-10-22). With isolcpus on all eight the scheduler stops that migration. The SDK's perf lane expects workers on non-isolated cores ('The online cores outside isolcpus: the workers', the client's and the fake device's' [phoenix-crb-round5.txt, section 'tools/perf/records.py isolation rules']).

Message 2, 'one update since this morning' versus message 3 dated '21 October 2026 (morning)' with 'whenever you have a moment': the two messages give different urgency, and which is the later one is not certain from the files [requests.txt header gives only the supplied order]. Insufficient data; Jeremy must confirm whether the Friday 2026-10-23 deadline stands.

Confirmed accurate (no correction), message 3: 'Today the governor is schedutil and no cores are isolated.' Evidence: 'governors: 128 schedutil;' [phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpufreq] and 'isolated: ' empty [section cpu_summary]; Jeremy's own snapshot at 18:32 UTC agrees [phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section isol_before_summary: 'isolated: ""', 'governors: {"schedutil": "128 cpus"}'].

Confirmed accurate (no correction), message 2: 'the reboot that isolcpus needs'. A no-reboot alternative exists (a cgroup v2 cpuset isolated partition; 'cpuset' is an available controller but not enabled: 'subtree_control: cpu memory pids' [phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cgroups]), but it also needs root, leaves /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated empty (torvalds master drivers/base/cpu.c print_cpus_isolated() uses HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT), so core_isolated stays false, and gives no nohz_full.

Confirmed accurate for availability (precision note, no correction), message 1: 'Ubuntu 24.04's packages cover these.' The apt index has clang-18 ('1:18.1.3-1ubuntu1'), ninja-build ('1.11.1-2'), cmake 3.28.3 and python3.12 with headers; python3.11 has no package ('python3.11: ' empty candidate), but 3.12.3 meets '3.11+' [phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section tools]. clang-18 and ninja-build are not installed ('clang-18 not in PATH', 'ninja not in PATH') and installing them needs sudo, which the account lacks; the SDK side met the need with a user-level conda-forge toolchain instead [phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section toolchain_readme]. Status DONE holds.

terms_to_define.definition: The Arm server at 192.168.2.45 (Linux hostname 'ubuntu', DNS name ubuntu.positron.internal). Firmware calls it 'Phoenix Reference Server', vendor Arm Limited, EVT0 (an early engineering-validation board), BIOS AGI-CPU-CRB-v0.7.2. 128 cores, no SMT, 377 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.5. Jeremy's messages call it 'the Phoenix CRB' or 'Phoenix'.
Positron's software development kit: the C++ runtime, the compiler, the Python bindings and the test tools, staged on the host at ~/positron/src/phoenix-int (commit ead1e9a, from a git bundle).
Positron's accelerator board. The requested jobs do not use it, and none is attached to phoenix-crb.
The unprivileged local account (uid 1001) on phoenix-crb created for the SDK's runs. It has no usable sudo and a locked password.
The administrator account on phoenix-crb (uid 1000, the only member of group sudo). It holds a console session on tty1 since 2026-10-20 19:31 UTC.

The machine at 192.168.1.200 (DNS name alpha.positron.internal from Jibin's workstation). It held arm admin sessions on 20-21 Oct and about 50 positron-perf sessions during the staging on 2026-10-21 17:07-18:32 UTC. Its operator is not identified.

The SDK team's development host. It has the LAN address 192.168.2.39 (sw-dev-01.positron.internal) and the Tailscale address 100.124.2.53 (sw-dev-01.porgy-gecko.ts.net). It logged in to phoenix-crb as positron-perf four times on 2026-10-21, so that path works.
Jibin's workstation, 192.168.2.136. The inspection scripts ran from it, and arm sessions from it created the positron-perf account on 2026-10-21 00:56-05:14 UTC.

Linux 7.1.3-arm-agi-20260916-v0.7.2-g4dbc8bb88858, the running kernel, built by the board's supplier ('avadnaik@2paltra-216', Ubuntu gcc-14 PPA) with silicon workarounds. It lacks CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL and CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU. Its source is not on the host.
Ubuntu's 6.8.0-147-generic, installed by unattended-upgrades on 2026-10-15, never booted on this board. Its config has CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL=y and CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU=y.

A kernel boot parameter that removes the listed CPUs from the scheduler's load balancing ('domain' flag), so only tasks pinned there run there. It takes effect only at boot and cannot be undone at runtime. The 'managed_irq' flag steers managed interrupts away where their mask also holds housekeeping CPUs. The 'nohz' flag must not be used on this kernel: it drops the whole parameter.

A kernel feature (build option CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL, boot parameter nohz_full=) that stops the periodic scheduler tick on a CPU that runs a single task; a residual tick of about 1 per second remains. The running kernel does not have it built in. nohz_full CPUs get their RCU callbacks offloaded automatically.

A boot parameter (needs CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU) that moves RCU callback processing (RCU is read-copy-update, a kernel synchronization mechanism) off the listed CPUs onto 'rcuo' kernel threads. The running kernel lacks the option; a NO_HZ_FULL kernel selects it.

A hardware interrupt and the set of CPUs allowed to handle it. A managed interrupt (here each NVMe disk queue, one per CPU) is placed by the kernel and cannot be moved through /proc/irq. It fires only when I/O is submitted from that CPU.
The periodic timer interrupt the kernel uses for scheduling. This kernel has HZ=250, so a busy CPU gets one tick every 4 ms (measured: 1261 ticks in 5 s on CPU 121). Only nohz_full stops it.
Inter-processor interrupt: one CPU interrupting another, for example to run a function call or reschedule. CPUs 120-127 received 123,695 function-call IPIs since boot.

The kernel policy that picks a CPU's clock. schedutil follows the scheduler's load estimate (on this host between 1.6 GHz and 2.8 GHz) and leaves a mostly-sleeping thread's CPU at 1.6 GHz; performance always requests the maximum (2.8 GHz). Each CPU is its own policy here.
A clock above the nominal maximum. On this host highest_perf equals nominal_perf (140 units), so there is no boost range and the boost flag reads 0.

ACPI Collaborative Processor Performance Control, the interface through which the cpufreq driver asks firmware for a performance level; 1 unit = 20 MHz here (lowest 80 = 1.6 GHz, nominal and highest 140 = 2.8 GHz). feedback_ctrs are two counters per CPU (reference and delivered) whose deltas give the average delivered clock; the file is world-readable.

The runtime's one thread per instance, named positron-pass, that plans and binds each forward pass. It pins itself to the core given as pass_thread_core (CPU 127 in Jeremy's run). The SDK's counts gate holds it to no syscall and no allocation per measured pass.
One run of the model that produces the next token for each active user. Jeremy's 'each step' means one pass.
Time to first token: the delay from a request's arrival to its first output token.

The SDK test backend that stands in for the accelerator: a device thread posts each pass's completion at a modelled time taken from a timing table and computes nothing. The thread sleeps until 100 us before each retirement and then spins. The SDK does not pin it.

The fake device's self-check. Lateness is how late each completion was posted. The band is 0.2% of the shortest cohort period (2.5 us in churn-r1). When the MEAN lateness exceeds the band the record is void and the latency judge returns INFRA. churn-r1: mean 6.2 us, maximum 220 us.

terms_to_define.term: latency judge / INFRA / per-user latency gate
terms_to_define.definition: The SDK tool tools/conformance/latency_judge.py that grades a run against the registered gate 'per-user-latency.qwen3_5_0_8b.P-TP1'. Verdicts are PASS, FAIL or INFRA (the run is not a measurement). It requires only that the pass thread was pinned (pass_thread_core is an integer); it records isolcpus as a fact and does not require it.

terms_to_define.term: perf lane / perf host / counted runs
terms_to_define.definition: tools/perf/perf_lane.py, the SDK's host-timing lane for the TPS gate and the compile-0.8b gate. It refuses any host that lacks an online core in both isolcpus and nohz_full. 'Perf host' is phoenix-crb; the SDK's README says timings 'count only from the perf host'. A counted run is one whose figures the SDK keeps as evidence.

The demo's measurement lane (tools/conformance/demo_d17.py) on null_timing: D17 is the TPS gate's software-overhead target, D21 the per-user latency targets beside it. Its figures are advisory and count only from the perf host.

The SDK CI job 'run_scheduled_gate.sh churn': it builds the Qwen3.5-0.8B fixture, replays a request mix through the runtime on the fake device and runs the latency judge. churn-r1 is Jeremy's first run of it on phoenix-crb (2026-10-21 18:32-18:35 UTC, 168 s, verdict INFRA).
A field churn.py and demo_d17.py record: true only if the pass core appears in /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated, which lists only boot-time isolcpus CPUs. It was false in churn-r1.
A Linux command that restricts a process to a CPU list. Jeremy's job ran the whole label under 'taskset -c 120-127'.

A runtime (no reboot) way to remove CPUs from scheduler load balancing: enable the cpuset controller, create a cgroup with cpuset.cpus and cpuset.cpus.partition=isolated, and move processes into it. It needs root, does not show in /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated, gives no nohz_full, and does not persist across reboot.

The boot loader. GRUB_DEFAULT=saved plus grubenv's saved_entry keeps the vendor kernel as the default entry. Files in /etc/default/grub.d/ set GRUB variables; 50-cloudimg-settings.cfg overrides GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT, so new boot arguments go in a new drop-in via GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX, then update-grub.

Ubuntu's automatic package updater and the systemd timers that run it (6:00 and 18:00 UTC with up to 12 h random delay, so at any hour). They installed three stock kernels since 9 Oct and do not reboot by themselves here.
A network benchmark server started at boot on this host (an LSB init script).
The system activity collector. It runs every 10 min from both a systemd timer and /etc/cron.d/sysstat.
IBM Spectrum LSF, a batch job scheduler. The SDK's dev lane submits jobs to shared LSF workers from sw-dev-01; phoenix-crb runs no LSF.

A Linux real-time scheduling policy and the limit that allows it. The account's hard rtprio limit is 0, so chrt -f fails. The runtime does not request it today; the design spec mentions it for the interpreter core.
UEFI firmware signature enforcement for kernels. It is off on this host (efivar SecureBoot data byte 0), so a locally built kernel needs no signing.

The login history file, the command that prints it, and systemd's log. Non-interactive SSH commands appear only in the journal; as the account, the journal shows the user's own sshd session lines but not the root-only 'Accepted publickey' lines that name the key.
Jeremy's timezone (UTC-4, from his commit's -0400), Jibin's (UTC-7) and the host's (UTC). After 2026-11-01 the US offsets become UTC-5 and UTC-8.

A single file that carries a git repository's history. The SDK source on the host was fetched from ~/positron/src/phoenix-int.bundle, commit ead1e9a 'local integration for Phoenix evidence, never pushed', authored Jeremy Conner 2026-10-21 14:20:48 -0400.
A package manager and package repository used to install the user-level toolchain (clang 18.1.8, CMake 3.31.6, Ninja 1.13.2, gcc 13.3.0) without sudo, matching sw-dev-01's lock.
The small model (1.7 GB of weights staged under ~/positron/weights) and the placement scheme the churn job compiles it on.

(1) The sampling unit tests: no test run is recorded (the three build logs match 'sampling' only on compile lines, the build job's targets were '_positron_core positron-harness positron-cpuref', and no ctest/pytest/LastTest.log file exists under ~/positron; host checks 2026-10-22); status unknown, a question for Jeremy. (2) The timed compile: tools/conformance/README.md line 16 says the compile-0.8b gate runs on 'the perf lane, on the perf host (spec §12.2), which does not run it yet'; no compile wall time is recorded; status not done. (3) 'One job at a time': no host-side mechanism; the perf lane has a lock, the churn script none. Implicit: message 2 asks for a status reply, and message 3's 'whenever you have a moment' conflicts with message 2's Friday deadline (order uncertain).

A1 (account DONE): agree, and two gaps close. The system journal (read as the account 2026-10-22) shows positron-perf sessions from 192.168.2.39 at 17:07:35, 18:22:31, 18:23:08 and 18:27:27 UTC and about 50 sessions from 192.168.1.200 between 17:07 and 18:32 UTC on 2026-10-21 (for example 'sshd[8158]: Disconnected from user positron-perf 192.168.1.200 port 55041' at 18:11:12 UTC, when ~/positron was created). DNS on Jibin's workstation resolves 192.168.2.39 to sw-dev-01.positron.internal (sw-dev-01 also has the Tailscale address 100.124.2.53) and 192.168.1.200 to alpha.positron.internal. So G2 (sw-dev-01 reaches 192.168.2.45:22) is resolved: it does. G6 is half resolved: the staging came from 'alpha' and sw-dev-01; which key was used stays unknown (sshd's 'Accepted publickey' lines are root-only). The draft's F17 'the host cannot resolve sw-dev-01' is true only because the host uses 8.8.8.8, not the positron.internal resolver. Who operates 'alpha' is insufficient data; it also held the arm admin sessions of 20-21 Oct.

A3 (toolchain DONE 'approved by Jeremy'): agree on DONE. The approval is self-reported in the SDK side's README ('approved by Jeremy that day', phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section toolchain_readme), not evidence from Jeremy.

A5 (no sudo / no outbound): agree it is not a blocker. Addition: the staging used the host's outbound network (23 pip 'Downloading' lines in work/venv-setup/pip-install.log, conda-forge fetches in work/toolchain-setup/create.log; phoenix-crb-round3.txt, section src_work_venvs), so 'we copy everything in' was not followed; nobody should firewall the host to match the sentence. Also note the rtprio hard limit 0 (SCHED_FIFO refused): not needed by the runtime today, but the design spec mentions SCHED_FIFO for the interpreter core (phoenix-crb-round5.txt, docs grep, design-12-repository.md line 182); raising it is a root change to limits.conf.

A6 (governor: root, no reboot): agree, with four additions. (1) 'No boost' is already satisfied by firmware ('highest_perf=140', 'nominal_perf=140', phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section cpufreq), not by a setting. (2) A live write does not survive the P2 reboot ('CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_DEFAULT_GOV_SCHEDUTIL=y', section kernel_config), so 'cpufreq.default_governor=performance' on the command line or a boot unit is required, not optional. (3) New measured evidence that the scope must include the run's other CPUs: over the 34 samples of churn-r1 (isol.samples.jsonl, host 2026-10-22) cpu124 and cpu125 were at 1,600,000 kHz in 34 of 34, cpu120 and cpu126 in 33 of 34, cpu121 and cpu123 in 31 of 34, cpu122 in 29 of 34, while cpu127 was at 2,800,000 kHz in 26 of 34. The fake device thread runs on those 1.6 GHz CPUs. Under the perf lane the workers and device run on 0-119 instead (records.py choose_cores). Host-wide performance is the one setting that fits both; the draft's 'nice-to-have: host-wide or 120-127' should become the default. (4) Delivered clock over a full run is unmeasured (3 s only, F7); feedback_ctrs deltas during a run give it without root.

A7 (isolcpus plus 'isolcpus=domain,managed_irq + irqaffinity' keeps IRQs off): partly disagree. The 16 interrupts that touch 120-127 are the NVMe queues nvme0q119-126 and nvme1q119-126 with a single-CPU mask each (phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section interrupts). The kernel-parameters doc (isolcpus= managed_irq, kernel.org, read 2026-10-22) says that when 'a queue's affinity mask contains only isolated CPUs then this parameter has no effect on the interrupt routing decision'; such interrupts 'are only delivered when tasks running on those isolated CPUs submit IO'. So managed_irq does not move them, and irqaffinity= applies only to non-managed IRQs. The timer tick (1261 per 5 s busy) and IPIs stay without nohz_full. 'IRQs kept off' is therefore only partly achievable; the after-reboot check is a /proc/interrupts delta on 120-127 during a run. Two confirmations for P2: isolcpus=domain does remove the CPUs from unbound workqueues (torvalds master kernel/workqueue.c workqueue_init_early(): 'restrict_unbound_cpumask("HK_TYPE_DOMAIN", housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN))'), answering P2's open question with yes; and the 'nohz' flag of isolcpus must not be used (S2 confirmed in kernel/sched/isolation.c: housekeeping_setup() returns 0 after 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported', dropping the whole parameter). One caveat from the docs: a 'domain' isolated CPU cannot be returned to the scheduling domains at runtime.

A7 / P1c (cpuset partition fallback): the draft understates three differences. (1) /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated stays empty, because torvalds master drivers/base/cpu.c print_cpus_isolated() prints the complement of 'housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT)', the boot-time set only (the 7.1 source itself was not checked); so churn.py and demo_d17.py record core_isolated=false. (2) The cpuset controller must first be enabled in /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control ('-rw-r--r-- 1 root root', host 2026-10-22; today 'cpu memory pids'), and the job's processes must be written into the partition cgroup by root or the cgroup delegated to positron-perf; taskset is not enough. (3) Nothing persists across reboot. P1c should be labelled 'does not give core_isolated' so Jeremy can decide (new D5).

A8 (nohz_full not possible; rebuild): agree. Additions: (1) Secure Boot is off (efivar SecureBoot data byte 0, host 2026-10-22), so a rebuilt kernel needs no signing. (2) The vendor kernel source is not on the host: /usr/src/linux-headers-7.1.3-... holds only 'Makefile Module.symvers arch include scripts', no kernel/ directory, 36 .c files (host 2026-10-22); 'building on the box' needs the source from the provider first, so G1 stays open. (3) The vendor kernel was built by 'avadnaik@2paltra-216' with 'gcc-14 (Ubuntu 14.3.0-12ubuntu1~24~ppa1)' (phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section boot_and_kernels, uname version string), not with /opt/arm-svk, so the arm-svk KERNEL_CC hint is suggestive, not proof of the provider's build setup. (4) Wording of S1: nohz_full= IS registered on every kernel (isolation.c has no #ifdef around '__setup("nohz_full=", ...)'); it is rejected at runtime and dropped. rcu_nocbs= is unregistered (RCU_NOCB_CPU absent). Net effect as the draft says: both ignored. (5) In torvalds master kernel/time/Kconfig the NO_HZ_FULL block lists 'select NO_HZ_COMMON', 'select RCU_NOCB_CPU', 'select IRQ_WORK', 'select CPU_ISOLATION' and no 'select VIRT_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GEN' (S6 said it is selected automatically); whoever builds the kernel should check the resulting .config for CONFIG_VIRT_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GEN=y and CONFIG_CONTEXT_TRACKING_USER=y. Unverified for 7.1.

A9 (nothing else running): agree, with specifics. The SDK's own quiet rule is narrower than 'nothing running': tools/perf/host_facts.sh (host 2026-10-22) flags other uids' processes at '$4 + 0 >= 5.0' percent CPU and a CI runner process ('Runner[.]Listener|actions-runne[r]|runsv[c][.]sh'), and records.py has 'LOAD_MAX = 0.5'; netperf and the apt timers would not trip it unless they burn 5% of a CPU at the facts snapshot. The draft's pause list is still prudent: apt-daily's 12 h random delay on a 6:00/18:00 UTC schedule means it can run at any hour (last run 21:57 UTC on 21 Oct); sysstat runs from both the timer and /etc/cron.d/sysstat, so both must be stopped; fstrim fires Mon 2026-10-26 00:27 UTC (Sunday 17:27 PDT). During churn-r1 the only non-harness processes seen on 120-127 were the job's own python processes (isol.samples.jsonl 'foreign_running_on_watch'). The reservation rule must include the arm console session (tty1 since 20 Oct 19:31 UTC) and whoever operates 'alpha' (192.168.1.200), which held arm sessions of 2 to 4 h on 20-21 Oct.

A10 ('counted runs Mon 10-26: achievable WITHOUT nohz_full'): disagree with 'achievable'. The Friday host setup is achievable; a counted run is not shown to be. churn-r1's INFRA verdict came from the fake device's MEAN lateness (6.2 us) exceeding its band (2.5 us), not from missing isolation; the void rule is on the mean (docs/null-timing.md line 87, record.h line 45, host 2026-10-22). The device thread is unpinned (backends/ has no affinity call) and ran on CPUs 120-126, which sat at 1.6 GHz. Whether governor plus isolcpus brings the mean under 2.5 us is unmeasured (G3). If the counted tool is tools/perf, the current kernel never passes. A10 should read 'setup achievable; counted-run validity unproven until a re-run after P1a', and the plan should test the governor alone first (root, no reboot) by re-running ~/positron/runs/ev3-churn-job.sh and reading device late_mean_s, which separates the governor effect from the isolcpus effect before the reboot.

D ('Not to start ... with the arm account'): agree, with two preconditions made explicit. Evidence that Jibin's side holds the arm credentials: arm sessions from 192.168.2.136 (claude-agentsrv) at 00:24-05:14 UTC on 21 Oct, during which the positron-perf home (00:56 UTC) and the sudoers drop-in (05:12 UTC) were created (phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section logins; phoenix-crb-followup.txt, section services_detail). The P2 reboot must be coordinated with the open tty1 console session ('arm tty1 Oct 20 19:31') and with 'alpha' (192.168.1.200), a second machine that holds arm sessions.

D1 ('He pre-approved workarounds'): overstated. Message 2 says 'tell me and we'll work around it', a commitment to decide together, not a pre-approval. But message 2 also says 'The rest of the list can follow later', so a Friday setup without nohz_full and rcu_nocbs is within what he already accepted. The message to him should say that nohz_full needs a different kernel, since his message 3 assumes a reboot is enough, and should ask whether the Friday deadline still stands given message 3's 'whenever you have a moment' and the unclear order of messages 2 and 3.

D2 (which tool gates the counted runs): agree it is the one decision that changes the critical path, and the evidence narrows it. Message 2 names 'per-user latency runs'; churn-r1's gate is 'per-user-latency.qwen3_5_0_8b.P-TP1' judged by latency_judge.py (phoenix-crb-round4.txt, section rejudge_summary), whose isolated() returns true whenever pass_thread_core is an integer (lines 1166-1169, host 2026-10-22); churn.py and demo_d17.py only record core_isolated as a fact. The README's 'count only from the perf host' refers to the host (phoenix-crb), not to tools/perf. tools/perf (TPS gate host timing and the compile-0.8b gate) is the only code that demands isolcpus plus nohz_full. So D2 should be phrased 'confirm the demo numbers come from the latency judge or D17 lane, not from tools/perf'. Latency judge: P1-P2 suffice, subject to the lateness measurement (G3). tools/perf: the kernel rebuild (P4) must land before 5 Nov.

D3 (CPU map): agree, and the evidence is stronger than the draft states. During churn-r1 the harness threads moved across all of 120-126 ('positron-harnes' sampled on CPUs 120, 121, 122, 123, 124, 125 and 126; 'positron-scrub' on 123, 124 and 126; isol.samples.jsonl, host 2026-10-22), because churn.py gives them the mask 120-126 ('os.sched_setaffinity(0, cpus)', phoenix-crb-round5.txt, placement() body) and worker_thread.cpp leave_pass_cpu() only clears the pass CPU from the mask. With isolcpus=domain on all of 120-127 that migration stops and each thread stays where it first lands. The two tools differ: churn keeps the other threads inside 120-126, records.py choose_cores puts them on 0-119 plus one isolated core. Isolating all of 120-127 fits the perf lane's model and not churn's taskset. Recommend as the default: isolate only the pass core(s) (for example 126-127) and reserve 120-125 by agreement, unless Jeremy pins each thread. Note isolcpus=domain cannot be undone at runtime, so the choice should be made before the reboot.

D4 (windows and clock rule): agree it needs Jeremy, but it blocks only the scheduling of windows and the acceptance rule, not P1-P2. Add the DST note: after 2026-11-01 Jibin is at UTC-8 and Jeremy at UTC-5, so the 5 Nov demo windows differ from October's by one hour.

New D5 (missing from the draft): if the reboot cannot happen by Friday, Jeremy must say whether the cpuset-partition fallback, which leaves core_isolated=false and needs root to place his processes in the cgroup, is acceptable for the 26 Oct runs.

New D6 (missing from the draft): where the fake device thread should run and whether to pin it. The SDK pins only the pass thread (pass_loop.cpp) and makes workers leave the pass CPU (worker_thread.cpp); backends/ has no affinity call (host 2026-10-22). Its mean lateness is the void criterion, so its placement decides whether runs count, and that is harness code on Jeremy's side. The host-side counterpart is the governor scope (host-wide), which is Jibin's decision and needs no input from Jeremy.

Nice-to-have 'confirm which login path he uses': now mostly answered by the journal and DNS (sessions from sw-dev-01 at 192.168.2.39 and from 'alpha' at 192.168.1.200); only the laptop path (the DESKTOP-V2B1166 key) and the identity of 'alpha' remain open, and nothing blocks on them.

findings.dimension: KERNEL AND CPU ISOLATION (isolcpus / nohz_full / rcu_nocbs / irqaffinity on the vendor kernel 7.1.3-arm-agi, the three nohz_full routes, the cgroup v2 cpuset alternative, GRUB mechanics, CPU split for Jeremy's threads, proposed command lines and verification)

findings.claim: The running vendor kernel 7.1.3-arm-agi has CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION=y, CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL not set and no CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU, so it supports isolcpus=domain, isolcpus=managed_irq and irqaffinity= but cannot provide nohz_full or rcu_nocbs on any reboot.
findings.evidence: phoenix-crb-inspection.txt, section '=== kernel_config ===': 'CONFIG_NO_HZ_IDLE=y', '# CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL is not set', 'CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION=y', '# CONFIG_RCU_EXPERT is not set' (no RCU_NOCB_CPU line). Host /boot/config-7.1.3-arm-agi-...: line 95 '# CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL is not set', line 144 'CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION=y', line 151 '# CONFIG_RCU_EXPERT is not set'. Linux v7.1.3 kernel/rcu/Kconfig lines 274-278: 'config RCU_NOCB_CPU ... depends on RCU_EXPERT || NO_HZ_FULL'. v7.1.3 kernel/sched/build_utility.c lines 100-102: '#ifdef CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION # include "isolation.c"'. v7.1.3 kernel/sched/isolation.c lines 325-339 parse the flags 'nohz,', 'domain,', 'managed_irq,'. Vendor headers /usr/src/linux-headers-7.1.3-.../include/linux/sched/isolation.h define the same HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT / HK_TYPE_DOMAIN / HK_TYPE_MANAGED_IRQ / HK_TYPE_KERNEL_NOISE enum as upstream v7.1.3, so the upstream v7.1.3 code read below applies to the vendor build.
findings.implication: Friday's setup on this kernel can deliver scheduler-domain isolation plus IRQ steering only; nohz_full/rcu_nocbs need a different kernel build (K6).
findings.action: Plan P2 on the current kernel with isolcpus=domain,managed_irq plus irqaffinity only; do not put nohz_full= or rcu_nocbs= on the current kernel's command line (see K2).

findings.claim: On the running kernel 'nohz_full=' is a registered boot parameter that is refused with the dmesg warning 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported. Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL' and then reported as unknown, 'rcu_nocbs=' is not registered at all and is only reported as unknown, and the 'nohz' flag of isolcpus= makes the kernel drop the WHOLE isolcpus= setting (domain and managed_irq included).
findings.evidence: Linux v7.1.3 kernel/sched/isolation.c lines 304-312: 'static int __init housekeeping_nohz_full_setup(char *str) { ... flags = HK_FLAG_KERNEL_NOISE; return housekeeping_setup(str, flags); } __setup("nohz_full=", housekeeping_nohz_full_setup);' (compiled under CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION, not CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL). Lines 211-216: 'if ((flags & HK_FLAG_KERNEL_NOISE) && !(housekeeping.flags & HK_FLAG_KERNEL_NOISE)) { if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL)) { pr_warn("Housekeeping: nohz unsupported." " Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL\n"); return 0; } }' — this return happens before the CPU list is parsed, and housekeeping_isolcpus_setup (lines 325-327, 365) passes the nohz flag into the same function. init/main.c lines 221-227: a __setup handler returning 0 leaves obsolete_checksetup() false; lines 903-904: pr_notice("Unknown kernel command line parameters \"%s\", will be passed to user space.\n"). kernel/rcu/tree_nocb.h line 16 '#ifdef CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU' ... line 71 '__setup("rcu_nocbs", rcu_nocb_setup);' ... line 1619 '#else /* #ifdef CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU */'.
findings.implication: Draft S1 is right about the effect (ignored) but wrong about the mechanism for nohz_full=; a mistaken 'isolcpus=nohz,domain,...' would silently remove all isolation, so the exact flag string matters.
findings.action: Use exactly 'isolcpus=domain,managed_irq,<cpus>' on the current kernel; after reboot run: dmesg | grep -E 'Housekeeping|Unknown kernel command line' and require no output.

findings.claim: isolcpus=domain alone on this 7.1.3 kernel removes the CPUs from scheduler domains (no load balancing), from unbound workqueues at boot, from preferred-affinity kthreads and from the timer-migration hierarchy, and lists them in /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated and /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset.cpus.isolated; it does not stop the 250 Hz tick, does not offload RCU callbacks and does not move delayed-work timers (those need the KERNEL_NOISE flag, i.e. nohz_full).
findings.evidence: v7.1.3 kernel/workqueue.c lines 7971-7979 (workqueue_init_early): 'cpumask_copy(wq_unbound_cpumask, cpu_possible_mask); restrict_unbound_cpumask("HK_TYPE_DOMAIN", housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN)); ... cpumask_andnot(wq_isolated_cpumask, cpu_possible_mask, housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN));' and line 7517 'DEVICE_ATTR_RO(cpumask_isolated)'. kernel/kthread.c lines 340-347 use 'housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN)' for kthread preferred affinity; include/linux/sched/isolation.h: 'HK_TYPE_KTHREAD = HK_TYPE_DOMAIN'. kernel/time/timer_migration.c lines 465-470: 'tmigr_is_isolated(int cpu) ... return (!housekeeping_cpu(cpu, HK_TYPE_DOMAIN) && housekeeping_cpu(cpu, HK_TYPE_KERNEL_NOISE));' and lines 1618-1634 'late_initcall(tmigr_init_isolation)'. drivers/base/cpu.c lines 293-294: isolated = cpu_possible_mask minus housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT). kernel/cgroup/cpuset.c lines 3705-3707: isolated_cpus initialised from HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT. kernel/sched/core.c line 1269-1275: get_nohz_timer_target() tests HK_TYPE_KERNEL_NOISE and walks the arming CPU's sched domains (which exclude isolated CPUs); kernel/workqueue.c lines 2569-2573: delayed work timers move only 'if (housekeeping_enabled(HK_TYPE_TIMER))' (TIMER is an alias of KERNEL_NOISE). Measured tick today: phoenix-crb-round3.txt '=== residual_tick_under_load ===': 'busy 5 s: arch_timer=1261 all_irqs=1264 (HZ=250 would give 1250 ticks in 5 s)'. Doc: v7.1.3 Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt isolcpus 'domain: Isolate from the general SMP balancing and scheduling algorithms. Note that performing domain isolation this way is irreversible'.
findings.implication: P2's open question ('isolcpus=domain also excludes the CPUs from unbound workqueues? — verify') is answered yes; the remaining noise on an isolated busy CPU under this kernel is the 250 Hz tick (one interrupt every 4 ms), function-call IPIs and RCU softirq work, which only a NO_HZ_FULL kernel removes.
findings.action: After the P2 reboot verify: cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset.cpus.isolated; cat /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask (bits of the isolated CPUs clear) and cpumask_isolated (bits set); ps -eo tid,psr,comm -L | awk '$2>=126' (only per-CPU kthreads plus the test); repeat the round3 arch_timer count during a pinned spin and expect still about 1250 ticks per 5 s.

findings.claim: irqaffinity=<list> sets the default affinity for every non-managed IRQ (the boot CPU is always kept in it); isolcpus=managed_irq cannot move the per-CPU NVMe queue interrupts on CPUs 120-127 because their masks contain a single isolated CPU, but those interrupts fire only for I/O submitted from that CPU; writing smp_affinity of a managed IRQ fails with EPERM (not EIO) on v7.1.3.
findings.evidence: v7.1.3 kernel/irq/irqdesc.c lines 28-39: 'irq_affinity_setup ... cpulist_parse(str, irq_default_affinity); /* Set at least the boot cpu ... */ cpumask_set_cpu(smp_processor_id(), irq_default_affinity); return 1; } __setup("irqaffinity=", irq_affinity_setup);'. kernel/irq/proc.c lines 143-144: 'if (!irq_can_set_affinity_usr(irq) || no_irq_affinity) return -EPERM;'. kernel-parameters.txt isolcpus managed_irq: 'If a queue's affinity mask contains only isolated CPUs then this parameter has no effect on the interrupt routing decision, though interrupts are only delivered when tasks running on those isolated CPUs submit IO.' Host state, phoenix-crb-inspection.txt '=== interrupts ===': 'default_smp_affinity: ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff', 'TOTAL irq dirs parsed: 452 with effective affinity touching 120-127: 16' (all nvme0q119-126 / nvme1q119-126, one CPU each), '196 0' effective on CPU 0, bnxt_en TxRx queues on 0-63.
findings.implication: Today nothing but NVMe queues, the per-CPU timer and IPIs targets 120-127, so irqaffinity= is insurance against future devices (for example the Asimov cards) rather than a fix for a present problem; the pass thread does no disk I/O, so its NVMe queue stays silent.
findings.action: Add 'irqaffinity=0-125' (variant A) or 'irqaffinity=0-119' (variant B) with the isolcpus argument; after reboot: cat /proc/irq/default_smp_affinity (expect 3fffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff for 0-125) and: for i in /proc/irq/[0-9]*; do printf '%s %s\n' "$(cat $i/effective_affinity_list)" "$(basename $i)"; done | awk '$1>=126' (expect only the nvme queue lines).

findings.claim: Booting the installed stock 6.8.0-147-generic kernel is an untested path on this EVT0 board: it has never booted here, it certainly lacks the vendor-only GIC 'AGI CPU A0' quirk, and it lacks two errata the vendor config enables (4311569 'SI L1 premature CMO completion', 4193714); the 'Broken broadcast TLBI completion' workaround, however, is upstream code (ARM64_WORKAROUND_REPEAT_TLBI via CONFIG_ARM64_ERRATUM_4118414, covering Neoverse-V3AE) and the Ubuntu 6.8 config also enables 4118414, so draft F4's TLBI argument is weaker than stated.

MIDR_ALL_VERSIONS(MIDR_NEOVERSE_V3AE)'; v6.8 cpu_errata.c line 520 names the same capability 'Qualcomm erratum 1009, or ARM erratum 1286807, 2441009' and v6.8 cputype.h has 0 matches for V3AE. Config diff vendor-vs-stock: vendor-only 'CONFIG_ARM64_ERRATUM_4311569=y', 'CONFIG_ARM64_ERRATUM_4193714=y'; v7.1.3 arch/arm64/Kconfig line 1127 'SI L1: 4311569: workaround for premature CMO completion erratum'. MIDR '0x410fd832' (dmesg 'Booting Linux on physical CPU 0x0000020000 [0x410fd832]') = Neoverse V3AE r0p2. Stock config also differs in CONFIG_HZ_1000=y, CONFIG_PREEMPT_DYNAMIC=y with CONFIG_PREEMPT_VOLUNTARY=y, CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_DEFAULT_GOV_ONDEMAND=y.
findings.implication: The stock kernel would give nohz_full without any kernel build, but with unknown silicon-level risk (GIC quirk missing) and a different timing baseline (HZ 1000, voluntary preemption, ondemand governor); it should stay out of the plan of record unless the kernel provider says the board boots it.
findings.action: Keep the vendor kernel as the plan of record (confirms F4's conclusion). If the stock kernel is ever tried, do it with grub-reboot (one-shot entry, GRUB_DEFAULT=saved already set) and a console on ttyAMA0, never by changing saved_entry first. Insufficient data on whether Ubuntu's 6.8.0-147 repeat-TLBI list includes V3AE: resolve with the Ubuntu noble source of arch/arm64/kernel/cpu_errata.c for tag Ubuntu-6.8.0-147.147 (launchpad returned HTTP 403 to this check).

findings.claim: On a NO_HZ_FULL kernel nohz_full CPUs are automatically RCU-offloaded, the residual 1 Hz scheduler tick runs remotely on a housekeeping CPU through the unbound workqueue (the nohz_full CPU itself gets no timer interrupt while one task runs in user space), and nohz_full= does not set the domain flag, so isolcpus=domain must be given as well to keep that workqueue and other unbound work off the isolated CPUs.
findings.evidence: v7.1.3 kernel/sched/core.c lines 5729-5780: 'static void sched_tick_remote(struct work_struct *work) ... /* Run the remote tick once per second (1Hz). ... */ ... queue_delayed_work(system_dfl_wq, dwork, HZ);' and lines 5783-5789 'sched_tick_start(int cpu) { ... if (housekeeping_cpu(cpu, HK_TYPE_KERNEL_NOISE)) return;'. kernel-parameters.txt isolcpus nohz: 'A residual 1Hz tick is offloaded to workqueues, which you need to affine to housekeeping through the global workqueue's affinity configured via the /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask sysfs file, or by using the 'domain' flag described below.' nohz_full= entry lines 4513-4521: 'The boot CPU will be forced outside the range to maintain the timekeeping. (printed with the 'rcu: ' prefix), isolation.c line 278 'Housekeeping: must include one present CPU neither in nohz_full= nor in isolcpus=domain'.
findings.implication: Draft S7's last sentence ('The tick still fires once per second on a nohz_full CPU') is wrong for this kernel generation: the 1 Hz work is remote. The command line for the rebuilt kernel must combine isolcpus=domain with nohz_full, and the boot CPU 0 must stay outside both sets (it does in every variant below).

findings.claim: systemd 255 on this host has no setting for cpuset.cpus.partition, but it does rewrite the root cgroup's cgroup.subtree_control with a '-' for every controller none of its units needs whenever it re-realizes the root slice (daemon-reload, daemon-reexec or a change of the needed controller set), which can silently drop a hand-enabled cpuset controller and dissolve a hand-made partition unless some systemd unit itself uses AllowedCPUs=.
findings.evidence: Host: 'systemd 255 (255.4-1ubuntu8.18)'; grep of /etc/systemd and /usr/lib/systemd/system for AllowedCPUs|CPUAffinity finds only the commented '#CPUAffinity=' at /etc/systemd/system.conf line 31. systemd v255 src/shared/cgroup-setup.c cg_enable_everywhere(): 'r = cg_get_path(SYSTEMD_CGROUP_CONTROLLER, p, "cgroup.subtree_control", &fs); ... for (c = 0; c < _CGROUP_CONTROLLER_MAX; c++) { ... s[0] = FLAGS_SET(mask, bit) ? '+' : '-'; ... write_string_stream(f, s, ...)' with the comment 'If we can't turn off a controller, leave it on in the reported resulting mask. This happens for example when we attempt to turn off a controller up in the tree that is used down in the tree.' src/core/cgroup.c unit_get_enable_mask(): 'mask = unit_get_members_mask(u); mask &= u->manager->cgroup_supported;' and unit_realize_cgroup_now_enable() recursing to 'slice = UNIT_GET_SLICE(u); if (slice) { r = unit_realize_cgroup_now_enable(slice, state);' (up to the root slice, whose cgroup path is the cgroup root). man systemd.resource-control (v255 xml) lists 'AllowedCPUs=' and 'StartupAllowedCPUs=' and contains no cpuset partition setting.
findings.implication: Draft S4's 'systemd does not manage cpuset.cpus.partition itself' is right, but 'must be written by hand' understates the interference: without an AllowedCPUs= property somewhere, the no-reboot partition can vanish on the next daemon-reload; this is a code reading, not a test on this host.

Conclusion (untested, not plan of record) stands: no stock-kernel boot in wtmp and the GIC 'AGI CPU A0' quirk is vendor-only (0 matches in upstream v6.8 and v7.1.3). But 'Broken broadcast TLBI completion' is upstream (ARM64_WORKAROUND_REPEAT_TLBI, erratum 4118414 covers Neoverse-V3AE) and the Ubuntu 6.8 config enables 4118414 and knows the V3AE MIDR, so that workaround is probably present in the stock kernel (V3AE coverage unverified). The vendor config also enables errata 4311569 and 4193714 which the stock config lacks.

Re-read on 2026-10-22: isolated empty, nohz_full absent, cpuset.cpus.isolated empty, subtree_control 'cpu memory pids'; additionally /sys/devices/system/cpu/housekeeping exists (new in this kernel) and is empty.
1261 arch_timer interrupts in 5 s on a busy CPU = HZ 250; only a NO_HZ_FULL kernel stops it (the 1 Hz residual then runs remotely on a housekeeping CPU).
16 managed NVMe queue IRQs are the only device IRQs on 120-127; the managed_irq flag cannot move single-CPU masks, and those queues fire only for I/O submitted from that CPU.
Workqueue cpumask all CPUs, cpumask_isolated present and zero (checked again 2026-10-22); scope limited to the workqueue statement.

churn.py reads /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated, which on 7.1.3 reflects boot-time isolcpus only (HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT), so a cpuset partition never satisfies it; records.py needs isolated AND nohz_full.

nohz_full= IS registered (isolation.c __setup under CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION) and is refused with 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported. Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL', then listed under 'Unknown kernel command line parameters'; rcu_nocbs= is indeed unregistered (tree_nocb.h under #ifdef CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU). Net effect (ignored) is as the draft said.
Exact warning text verified; the refusal returns before the CPU list is parsed, so the nohz flag discards domain and managed_irq too.
