findings.implication: netserver is the one item that lets a third party load the host without logging in; stop it for the window. smartd is harmless after isolation (admin queue on CPU 0) and may stay. sysstat timers are pure overhead right now; if Jibin wants sar's per-CPU history as evidence instead, set ENABLED="true" rather than disabling.
findings.action: sudo systemctl stop netperf.service && sudo update-rc.d netperf disable  (the unit is generated from /etc/init.d/netperf, so update-rc.d keeps it off across the P2 reboot); restore: sudo update-rc.d netperf enable && sudo systemctl start netperf.service. Optional: sudo systemctl stop smartmontools.service (restore with start). Decide on sysstat: either leave the two timers disabled (N8 list) or enable collection: sudo sed -i 's/^ENABLED=.*/ENABLED="true"/' /etc/default/sysstat.

findings.claim: RCU kernel threads today: rcu_preempt (the grace-period thread, pid 15) and rcu_exp_gp_kthread_worker (pid 17) may run on any CPU (allowed 0-127); the eight rcu_exp_par_gp_kthread_worker/1..8 are each confined to one 16-CPU leaf, and worker/8 (pid 586) is allowed 112-127, which overlaps the isolated set; rcu_tasks_kthread and rcu_tasks_rude_kthread are allowed 0-127. RCU callback invocation currently runs in the RCU softirq on the CPU that queued the callback (160,423 RCU softirqs on 120-127 since boot, mostly during the churn job). rcu_nocbs=120-127 (only possible on the rebuilt kernel; nohz_full implies it) would move callback invocation to rcuop/N and rcuog/N kthreads that run on housekeeping CPUs; it would NOT remove the tick, the expedited-GP IPIs (N4), or the need for the CPU to report quiescent states. With isolcpus=domain the unbound RCU kthreads are kept off 120-127 in practice (no scheduler domain contains those CPUs, and the kthread preferred-affinity code is present); with nohz_full the exclusion becomes explicit through the kernel-noise housekeeping mask.
findings.evidence: Host check 00:42 UTC: 'pid 15 rcu_preempt psr=4 allowed=0-127', 'pid 17 rcu_exp_gp_kthread_worker psr=64 allowed=0-127', 'pid 505 rcu_exp_par_gp_kthread_worker/7 psr=97 allowed=96-111', 'pid 586 rcu_exp_par_gp_kthread_worker/8 psr=0 allowed=112-127', 'pid 680 rcu_tasks_kthread psr=6 allowed=0-127', 'pid 681 rcu_tasks_rude_kthread psr=12 allowed=0-127'. phoenix-crb-inspection.txt === background ===: '--- rcu kernel threads / 15 79 rcu_preempt ... pid 15: rcu_preempt allowed=0-127 / pid 16: rcu_exp_par_gp_kthread_worker/1 allowed=0-15'; '--- softirqs totals on 120-127 ... RCU: 160423, TIMER: 183443, SCHED: 61651'. phoenix-crb-followup.txt === dmesg_greps ===: 'rcu: Preemptible hierarchical RCU implementation.', 'rcu: Adjusting geometry for rcu_fanout_leaf=16, nr_cpu_ids=128'. === kernel_config ===: 'CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU=y', '# CONFIG_RCU_EXPERT is not set', no CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU line. kernel-parameters.txt rcu_nocbs=: 'prevents such CPUs' callbacks from being invoked in softirq context', callbacks go to 'rcuox/N' kthreads; nohz_full= CPUs 'have their RCU callbacks offloaded'. Host kallsyms: 'kthread_affine_preferred', 'kthreads_online_cpu' present; 'rcu_nocb_setup' absent.
findings.implication: Draft F11/A8 are right that rcu_nocbs needs the rebuilt kernel. The practical gain of rcu_nocbs on the pass CPU is small unless the pass thread itself does kernel work that queues callbacks (file I/O, sockets); the fake device/workers on 120-126 do. The exp-par worker/8 overlap with 120-127 is cosmetic after isolcpus=domain.
findings.action: When the rebuilt kernel is available (P4): add 'nohz_full=120-127 rcu_nocbs=120-127' and verify: dmesg | grep -E 'NO_HZ: Full dynticks|rcu:.*Offload'; ps -eo pid,comm | grep -E 'rcuo[pg]/12[0-7]'; cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/nohz_full (expect 120-127). Until then nothing to do for RCU.

findings.claim: A read-only quiet-window proof that positron-perf can run exists in parts (Jeremy's isol.py snap/sample/diff) and needs four additions: per-IRQ-line deltas (isol.py sums all lines per CPU, so tick, IPI and NVMe cannot be told apart), the pass thread's own preemption counters (/proc/<tid>/sched 'nr_involuntary_switches' and 'se.nr_migrations' are readable and were 0 for an untouched task; a pinned pass thread that is never preempted keeps nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches at 0 for the whole run), /proc/stat user+system on each watched CPU compared with the harness's own CPU time (any excess is foreign work; 5 s ps snapshots miss short tasks, and /proc/schedstat does not exist on this kernel), and a check that the timers are paused. One caveat for the clock evidence: reading /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuN/acpi_cppc/feedback_ctrs (the method in draft F7) sends two function-call IPIs to CPU N per read because the AMU counters are read on the owning core via smp_call_function_single(); scaling_cur_freq (what isol.py samples) is IPI-free.

Host check: '/proc/self/sched: nr_switches 0, nr_voluntary_switches 0, nr_involuntary_switches 0, se.nr_migrations 0', 'nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches: 0'. phoenix-crb-round3.txt === residual_tick_under_load ===: 'head: cannot open /proc/schedstat'. Host host_facts.sh (tools/perf/host_facts.sh): 'others=$(ps -eo uid=,user:64=,pid=,pcpu=,comm= | awk ... $1 != me && $4 + 0 >= 5.0 ...)', 'load1=$(cut -d " " -f 1 /proc/loadavg)'; records.py: 'LOAD_MAX = 0.5 # the one-minute load average before a run, above which the host is not quiet'. arch/arm64/kernel/topology.c (mainline): counters_read_on_cpu(): 'return smp_call_function_single(cpu, func, val, 1);' used by cpc_read_ffh() for both the core and the constant counter; arch_freq_get_on_cpu() returns '-EAGAIN' ('No alternative to pull info from') without an IPI. phoenix-crb-followup.txt === cpufreq_extra === (draft F7): feedback_ctrs deltas used for the clock measurement. Host kallsyms: 'show_feedback_ctrs', 'cppc_get_perf_ctrs', 'cpc_read_ffh', 'cpu_read_corecnt'.
findings.implication: The proof can be produced without root and the pass criteria can be numeric: per idle isolated CPU over the run, arch_timer <= 5/s, IPI1 <= 0.5/s, NVMe queue lines 0, foreign threads none; on the pass CPU, arch_timer about 250/s x busy fraction, IPI1 about 0/s with timers paused, nr_involuntary_switches delta 0, se.nr_migrations delta 0; host load1 <= 0.5 before the run and 'others' empty (the perf lane's own rules). Clock sampling with feedback_ctrs must be sparse (for example once per 10 s, or only before/after) or it adds 2 IPIs per sample to the isolated CPU.
findings.action: Add to isol.py (Jeremy) or run beside it pinned to CPU 0 (taskset -c 0), before and after each timed run: (1) awk 'NR==1 || /arch_timer|^IPI|nvme[01]q(119|12[0-6])$/' /proc/interrupts and diff per CPU column 120-127 per line; (2) grep -E '^cpu(12[0-7]) ' /proc/stat before/after, compare user+system deltas with the sum over the harness's /proc/<pid>/task/*/stat utime+stime deltas; (3) for the pass thread: grep -E 'nr_involuntary_switches|se.nr_migrations' /proc/<tid>/sched before/after; (4) ps -eLo tid,psr,user,comm --no-headers | awk '$2>=120&&$2<=127&&$3!="root"' once per second, keep anything not the harness; (5) systemctl is-active apt-daily.timer apt-daily-upgrade.timer fwupd-refresh.timer; (6) before the run, Jeremy's hiccup in spin mode on the pass CPU for about 2 s, record the max gap in us as the direct stall figure. Sample feedback_ctrs at most every 10 s.

Time zones: host UTC, Jibin PDT (UTC-7), Jeremy EDT (UTC-4). A nightly default window of 01:00-13:00 UTC (18:00-06:00 PDT, 21:00-09:00 EDT) avoids both working days; Jeremy's staging so far ran at 17:00-19:00 UTC, inside his working day, so the window must be an agreement, not a fixed slot.
findings.action: Propose to Jeremy and adopt on the admin side: (1) the job writes /tmp/positron-perf.RUNNING with 'start_utc end_utc pid tag' at start and removes it at the end (world-readable; /tmp is sticky); (2) before any admin action, run: cat /tmp/positron-perf.RUNNING 2>/dev/null; ps -u positron-perf -o pid,etime,pcpu,comm --no-headers | awk '$3>0' and do nothing while either shows a run; (3) no package operations, builds, netperf, or reboots during the window; reboots announced 24 h ahead in the shared chat; (4) idle login sessions are allowed (the tty1 bash costs nothing), interactive commands are not; (5) Jeremy announces counted-run windows in UTC at least 2 h ahead and runs one job at a time (his own words). findings.claim: TLB shootdown on this arm64 host is not an IPI and cannot be isolated away: the kernel invalidates remote TLBs with broadcast TLBI instructions in hardware, and the 'Broken broadcast TLBI completion' feature in dmesg is the CPU erratum of CVE-2026-53354 (Arm CVE-2025-10263), mitigated by ARM64_WORKAROUND_REPEAT_TLBI (the sequence TLBI;DSB is issued twice); no IPI-based TLB flush code is present in the running kernel. The cost to an isolated CPU is snoop traffic from any process on the host that unmaps or remaps memory, plus shared L3 (128 MiB, shared by all 128 CPUs) and DRAM bandwidth; the only mitigation is to keep the rest of the host idle during a run.
findings.evidence: phoenix-crb-followup.txt === dmesg_greps ===: '[ 0.000000] CPU features: detected: Broken broadcast TLBI completion'. Host kallsyms: 'arm64_repeat_tlbi_list' present; no symbol matching 'ipi_flush_tlb*' or 'flush_tlb_ipi*'; 'flush_tlb_kernel_range' present (broadcast implementation). Web: Red Hat Bugzilla 2495939 / CVE-2026-53354 ('arm64: errata: Mitigate TLBI errata on various Arm CPUs'): 'a broadcast TLBI;DSB sequence may complete before the global observation of writes ... The existing ARM64_WORKAROUND_REPEAT_TLBI kernel feature is sufficient'. phoenix-crb-inspection.txt === topology_120_127 ===: 'index3 L3 Unified 131072K shared=0-127'.
findings.implication: The task's 'IPIs for TLB shootdown' category is empty on arm64; what remains in the 'nothing removes' set is: the SDK's own timer wakeups (N2), its own rescheduling IPIs and NVMe completions (N5), kernel text patching (module load, BPF) that wakes migration/N on all CPUs, and cache/memory-bandwidth sharing. Confidence medium because the vendor kernel source was not read; the symbol table and the public erratum description agree.
findings.action: No configuration. Add to the reservation rule: no module loads, no builds and no large memory jobs on CPUs 0-119 during a counted run (L3 and DRAM are shared by all 128 cores).

draft_verdicts.draft_item: F2 (kernel config: NO_HZ_FULL not set, no RCU_NOCB_CPU, CPU_ISOLATION=y, HZ=250, PREEMPT=y)
draft_verdicts.note: Config lines confirmed; kallsyms on the running kernel agrees: no tick_nohz_full_*, no rcu_nocb_*, no context_tracking_enabled; housekeeping_isolcpus_setup present.

draft_verdicts.draft_item: F9 (residual tick: 10 ticks/5 s idle, 1261/5 s busy; nohz_full would stop it; nothing on the current kernel can)
draft_verdicts.note: Re-measured 1264 and 1265 arch_timer in 5 s busy (253/s) and 25 in 5 s idle on CPU 121. Nuance: nohz_full reduces it to the residual 1 Hz tick plus the task's own timers, not to zero.

draft_verdicts.draft_item: F10 (only managed NVMe IRQs plus timer and IPIs touch 120-127; counts since boot; irqbalance absent)
draft_verdicts.note: Facts confirmed (16 NVMe vectors, 196 IRQs effective on CPU 0, 5.33 M arch_timer, 123,695 IPI1, 2,032 IPI0). Correction of meaning: 91.3 % of those interrupts (5.01 M of 5.49 M) were Jeremy's 173 s churn-r1 job's own hrtimer wakeups at 1.3-7.7 k/s per worker CPU, not host noise. The 'TxRx on CPUs 0-63' detail was not checkable from my sections (counts on 120-127 are 0, which suffices).

draft_verdicts.draft_item: F11 (background services and timers; Automatic-Reboot off; workqueue cpumask all CPUs; e2scrub no-op)
draft_verdicts.note: Confirmed with additions: fwupd-refresh runs hourly (not listed as such), apt-daily's 12 h random delay covers the whole day (ran 21:57 UTC 21 Oct), sysstat timers collect nothing (ENABLED=false, no sa files after 15 Oct), unattended-upgrades.service is only the shutdown hook, netserver pid 1861 is running, smartd polls every 30 min, no snaps installed, cron is a no-op. 'per-CPU interrupt deltas' line in the inspection is cumulative, not a delta.

draft_verdicts.draft_item: F18 (churn-r1: irqs_each_watch, busy shares, INFRA verdict)
draft_verdicts.note: Numbers re-read from round4; the interrupts per CPU are the job's own timer wakeups (N2); cpu127's lifetime user time (132.1 s) equals the job's busy time on it (131.6 s).

draft_verdicts.draft_item: F19 (isol.py / churn.py record core_isolated from /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated; perf lane needs isolcpus AND nohz_full)
draft_verdicts.note: Also read host_facts.sh: 'others' = other users' processes at >= 5 % CPU, load1 from /proc/loadavg, LOAD_MAX = 0.5; isol.py sums all IRQ lines per CPU (cannot separate tick/IPI/NVMe).

draft_verdicts.draft_item: F20 (arm console session since 2026-10-20 19:31 UTC; arm logins from 192.168.2.136 and 192.168.1.200)
draft_verdicts.note: The tty1 session is idle since 19:31:29 UTC 20 Oct (IdleHint=yes), owns one idle bash. 192.168.1.200 = 'alpha' also made 101 positron-perf logins 17:07-18:58 UTC 21 Oct (round6); its operator is unknown.

draft_verdicts.draft_item: S1 (nohz_full= and rcu_nocbs= would be reported as unknown parameters and ignored)
draft_verdicts.note: rcu_nocbs=: yes, unknown (no handler in kallsyms). nohz_full=: the handler housekeeping_nohz_full_setup exists (no #ifdef in isolation.c); the kernel parses it and refuses with 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported. Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL' in dmesg. Either way no effect.

draft_verdicts.draft_item: S2 (isolcpus=domain,managed_irq works; the nohz flag must not be used on this kernel)
draft_verdicts.note: Sharpened: housekeeping_setup() returns 0 before applying any flag, so 'isolcpus=nohz,domain,managed_irq,120-127' would lose domain and managed_irq as well.

draft_verdicts.draft_item: S3 (irqaffinity= generic; managed IRQs handled by isolcpus=managed_irq best effort; /proc writes fail EIO/EPERM; NVMe queue IRQ on CPU N only for I/O from CPU N)
draft_verdicts.note: All true in effect. Precision: v6.8 returns EIO, current mainline EPERM, vendor 7.1.3 not determined; isolcpus=managed_irq has NO effect on this host because every NVMe vector mask holds exactly one CPU (kernel doc: 'has no effect on the interrupt routing decision'); the 1:1 hctx-to-CPU mapping (hctx 118..125 -> CPU 120..127) was verified.

draft_verdicts.draft_item: S4 (cpuset isolated partition: no reboot, removes CPUs from unbound workqueues since 6.7, no nohz_full, does not move managed IRQs, not managed by systemd)
draft_verdicts.note: On this kernel the partition path calls housekeeping_update(): unbound workqueues, timer migration and kthread affinity are updated at runtime; HK_TYPE_MANAGED_IRQ is not (moot here). cpuset controller must first be added to cgroup.subtree_control (today: cpu memory pids). churn.py's core_isolated stays false on this path.

draft_verdicts.draft_item: S7 (nohz_full implies rcu_nocbs; residual 1 Hz tick; domain isolation only with isolcpus)

draft_verdicts.draft_item: A7 (isolated cores with IRQs kept off: possible with root + reboot, or partially without reboot)

draft_verdicts.draft_item: P1c (cpuset isolated partition + default_smp_affinity + move movable IRQs, non-persistent)
draft_verdicts.note: The partition part works (N7). The IRQ part is unnecessary: no movable IRQ is effective on 120-127 today, and the NVMe ones cannot and need not be moved.

draft_verdicts.draft_item: P2 (GRUB drop-in with isolcpus=domain,managed_irq,120-127 irqaffinity=0-119 ...; verify ... 'isolcpus=domain also excludes the CPUs from unbound workqueues? verify')
draft_verdicts.note: Yes: wq_unbound_cpumask is restricted by HK_TYPE_DOMAIN at boot (workqueue_init_early), and the timer-migration hierarchy excludes domain-isolated CPUs (tmigr_init_isolation present on this kernel). Expected /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask after reboot: 00ffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff. Do not add nohz_full=/rcu_nocbs= on this kernel (warnings only).

draft_verdicts.draft_item: P3 (hand-off note: known limitation no nohz_full; reservation rule; pre-run checklist, isol.py covers most)
draft_verdicts.note: Add two limitations: expedited-RCU IPIs reach the busy pass CPU on every service start/stop (N4), and feedback_ctrs reads IPI the target CPU twice per read (N11). isol.py needs per-line IRQ deltas, pass-thread preemption counters, /proc/stat cross-check and a timer-paused check (N11).

draft_verdicts.note: Restore outside a run window: the Persistent=true timers run their missed jobs immediately when re-enabled.

The '1264 and 1265 at 00:48 UTC' figures are not in any file. Kernel-side claims hold: /proc/kallsyms on the host has housekeeping_nohz_full_setup, housekeeping_isolcpus_setup and housekeeping_setup and lacks tick_nohz_full_setup, tick_nohz_full_running, context_tracking_enabled, rcu_nocb_setup, rcu_nocb_mask and rcu_init_nohz; mainline isolation.c has the unconditional '__setup("nohz_full=", housekeeping_nohz_full_setup);', the KERNEL_NOISE check as the first statement of housekeeping_setup() (before cpulist_parse), the pr_warn 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported.' followed by 'return 0;', 'err = 1;' only on success, and 'return 0;' on an invalid isolcpus flag. One correction: because the handler returns 0, init/main.c obsolete_checksetup() treats the parameter as not handled ('the setup function is invoked and its nonzero result returns true'), so unknown_bootoption() stores 'nohz_full=120-127' in PID 1's environment and print_unknown_bootoptions() lists it in 'Unknown kernel command line parameters "...", will be passed to user space.' Therefore nohz_full= produces BOTH the Housekeeping warning and the unknown-parameter notice; draft S1's wording was right for both parameters, and the analyst's S1 correction is only half right. The 'isolcpus=nohz,...' loss of domain and managed_irq is confirmed (the check precedes any mask application). dmesg today has 0 'Housekeeping' and 0 'Unknown kernel command line' lines (nothing on the cmdline yet).
verdicts.correction: A busy CPU takes about 252-253 arch_timer interrupts/s (files: 252.2/s and 251.6/s; my sample 253/s). On this kernel nohz_full= is parsed by housekeeping_nohz_full_setup(), refused with 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported. Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL', AND, because the handler returns 0, also listed in the 'Unknown kernel command line parameters' notice and passed to init's environment; rcu_nocbs= has no handler and gets only the unknown-parameter notice. Neither has any effect. 'isolcpus=nohz,...' would drop every flag of that isolcpus= setting.

verdicts.reason: Mechanism confirmed from source and host: tree_exp.h __sync_rcu_exp_select_node_cpus() takes 'snap = ct_rcu_watching_cpu_acquire(cpu);', marks 'if (rcu_watching_snap_in_eqs(snap))' CPUs done, computes 'mask_ofl_ipi = rnp->expmask & ~mask_ofl_test;' and sends 'ret = smp_call_function_single(cpu, rcu_exp_handler, NULL, 0);' ('/* IPI the remaining CPUs for expedited quiescent state. */'); the host kallsyms has rcu_exp_handler, synchronize_rcu_expedited, namespace_unlock and synchronize_net and lacks context_tracking_enabled. I reproduced the effect without starting any service: a 4 s pinned spin on CPU 121 received IPI1 +1 (control) versus +4 when three unprivileged 'unshare -Urm true' calls (a user+mount namespace torn down at exit; permitted on this host, rc=0) ran on another CPU during the spin, i.e. one function-call IPI to the busy CPU per namespace teardown; idle 3 s: +2. The specific numbers 0 / 25 / 2 from the 00:48 UTC timedatectl test and the '123,695 -> 132,061 in 55 min' background are not in any evidence file (unverifiable); my 01:14 UTC reading is IPI1 on120_127=139,072 (+15,377 since 23:47 UTC, including the checks' own IPIs), and systemd-timedated.service does have PrivateTmp=yes ProtectHome=yes ProtectSystem=strict (host). Caveat for interpretation: on an idle CPU, IPI1 also counts remote wake-ups of that CPU's own kthreads (the scheduler's wake-list path uses the function-call IPI), so idle IPI1 counts are not purely expedited RCU; on a busy CPU the expedited handler is the plausible source.

Drivers: vm.stat_interval = 1 (vmstat_update runs on a CPU up to once per second while its counters change), THP enabled=[always] with khugepaged scan_sleep_millisecs=10000, defrag=1, pages_collapsed=239, thp_fault_alloc 4690 (khugepaged's lru_add_drain_all() queues per-CPU drain work on CPUs with pending folio batches). Only nohz_full (quiet_vmstat) or a larger vm.stat_interval (root) reduce vmstat_update; measurement without root: before/after a run, diff voluntary_ctxt_switches of every kworker/127:* and of ksoftirqd/127 and migration/127, plus nr_involuntary_switches of the pass thread. 'snap list' is not a read-only command in effect: snapd.socket is active and enabled, so any snap command socket-activates snapd.service, which then tries to mount a 'partial' snap and fails on this kernel ('loop0: detected capacity change from 0 to 8' / 'Filesystem uses "xz" compression. This is not supported') and exits again. dmesg shows this at boot (12.7 s), at uptime 106578 s = 00:42:52 UTC 22 Oct (the analyst's host check ran 'snap list') and at 108508 s = 01:15:02 UTC (my check; snapd.service ActiveEnterTimestamp=Thu 2026-10-22 01:14:57 UTC, inactive again at 01:23 UTC). Pre-flight scripts must not run snap commands; if 'nothing else running' is strict, add snapd.socket to the pause list (disable --now) alongside snapd.snap-repair.timer. [host 01:23 UTC ssh check; host 01:21 UTC dmesg tail; phoenix-crb-inspection.txt === background === 'snapd=inactive', 'snapd=enabled']

The bnxt_en TxRx interrupts are all effectively serviced on CPU 0, not spread over CPUs 0-63: every sampled TxRx vector has smp_affinity_list 0-127 and effective_affinity_list 0, and 196 of the 452 IRQs are effective on CPU 0 (the host-wide distribution '196 0 / 3 64 / 2 99 ...' where the pairs are the two NVMe queues per CPU). Draft F10's 'sit on CPUs 0-63' is therefore wrong; network load concentrates on CPU 0 and whatever CPU the receiving process runs on. [host 01:14 UTC noise_check.out nvme_queues 'bnxt TxRx effective affinities'; phoenix-crb-inspection.txt === interrupts === effective_affinity_list distribution]

The fake device's poll interval is derived in code and sets a floor on the timer-wakeup rate of its CPU: null_timing.cpp:19 'constexpr std::int64_t kMinPollNs = 20'000, kMaxPollNs = 1'000'000;', :242 'shortest_T = std::min(kMaxPollNs * 4, to_ns(table->shortest_T_soft_s()))', :270 FakeDevice gets 'std::clamp(shortest_T / 4, kMinPollNs, kMaxPollNs)' as poll_ns, and fake_device.cpp:214 'std::int64_t sleep = poll_ns_;  // the whole sleep when nothing is queued'. So the device thread wakes 1,000-50,000 times per second while nothing is queued (4,000/s at a 1 ms shortest pass). Other timed sleeps: pool.cpp:394,418 'sleep_for(config_.idle_sleep)' (worker idle loop), scrub_worker.cpp:105,132 (same), pool.cpp:128 'sleep_for(poll_)', pass_loop.cpp:134 idle_nap/detached_nap and :213 'sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds{20})', waker.cpp:56 'sleep_cv_.wait_for(lock, options_.period, ...)', counts_page_map.cpp:63 1 ms. The managed NVMe vectors' /proc/irq/N/smp_affinity_list files are mode 0444 on the running kernel ('perms=444' for IRQ 176, 183, 304, 311), which is the newer genirq proc code where register_irq_proc() grants S_IWUSR only when irq_can_set_affinity_usr() is true; root can still open them (CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE) and the write handler returns -EPERM in that tree state. So the post-reboot root test in N5 should expect 'Operation not permitted'. [host 01:14 UTC noise_check.out nvme_queues; WebFetch kernel/irq/proc.c master]

verdicts.lens: LINUX-SEMANTICS verifier for the dimension "interrupts-noise" (tick, IPIs, managed IRQs, workqueues/kthreads under isolcpus=domain and cpuset isolated partitions, RCU, systemd timers). Sources: the six evidence files, kernel source on raw.githubusercontent.com (torvalds/linux master, tags v6.8 and v7.1), kernel admin-guide docs, and read-only re-checks on positron-perf@192.168.2.45 at 01:10-01:24 UTC on 22 Oct 2026 (two 4 s single-CPU spins, 100 sysfs reads, kallsyms/sysfs/systemctl reads; nothing written, no sudo). Running kernel treated as upstream-like 7.1 with the config in === kernel_config ===.

verdicts.reason: The interrupt-name semantics are right for arm64: IRQ 12 'GICv3 26 Level arch_timer' is the per-CPU clock-event line that carries both the HZ=250 tick and hrtimer expiries; the /proc/interrupts labels in the evidence are 'IPI0 ... Rescheduling interrupts', 'IPI1 ... Function call interrupts', 'IPI5 ... IRQ work interrupts'. Sums recomputed with irq_math.py: the per-CPU cumulative line sums to 5,487,292; arch_timer 5,327,444 = 97.1 %; IPI1 123,695 = 2.25 %; the NVMe queue lines on 120-127 sum to 33,539 = 0.61 %; idle rate 200/5 s/8 CPUs = 5.0 arch_timer/s per CPU, cpu121 alone 2.0/s; IPI1 3/5 s/8 = 0.075/s. The note that inspect.sh's 'per-CPU interrupt deltas 120-127 over the same 5 s' line is cumulative is correct: that awk reads /proc/interrupts once (inspect.sh, line beginning 'echo "--- per-CPU interrupt deltas'). My re-read at 01:20 UTC 22 Oct found 18 unbound kworkers (u528:0/1/3, u530, u532-u545) plus two rescuer threads (kworker/R-uas on 127, kworker/R-vfio-irqfd-cleanup on 126) plus rsyslog's 'in:imuxsock' thread on 120; '19' is a per-snapshot count, not a constant.

verdicts.reason: Arithmetic reproduced: job interrupts 5,010,908 of 5,487,292 cumulative = 91.3 %; cpu124 1,324,691/172.9 s = 7,661.6/s at 3.1 % busy where the tick explains at most 7.8/s; cpu127 236.3/s vs 0.7609 x 250 = 190.2/s; non-timer lines on 120-127 since boot total 159,595, so at least 4,851,313 of the job's interrupts were arch_timer. cpu127 user time 13212 USER_HZ ticks = 132.1 s vs 0.7609 x 172.9 s = 131.6 s. The semantic claim is right: neither isolcpus nor nohz_full suppresses a task's own hrtimer expiries (nohz_full only stops the periodic tick 'whenever possible'; the task's clock_nanosleep/futex timeouts still expire on its CPU). One cost statement is overstated.
verdicts.correction: 'on CPU 124 that is about 3 % of the CPU' conflates the threads' own run time with interrupt cost. /proc/stat cpu124 (=== cpu_activity ===: 'cpu124 322 0 238 10328308 29 158 21') gives irq = 158 ticks = 1.58 s of hardirq time since boot, versus 0.0314 x 172.9 s = 5.4 s busy during the job; so hardirq handling was at most 0.9 % of the job window (est. 1.58 s / 1,410,288 arch_timer = 1.1 us per interrupt), and the remaining ~2 % is the threads' own user+system time.

verdicts.reason: Measured tick rate confirmed: my 4 s pinned spin on CPU 125 took 1009 arch_timer = 252/s (control) and 1030/4 s with services starting; round3 had 1261 and 1258 per 5 s. Source confirmed: kernel/sched/isolation.c housekeeping_setup() tests '(flags & HK_FLAG_KERNEL_NOISE) && !(housekeeping.flags & HK_FLAG_KERNEL_NOISE)' then 'if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL)) { pr_warn("Housekeeping: nohz unsupported." " Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL\n"); return 0; }' before alloc_bootmem_cpumask_var/cpulist_parse, so with 'nohz' in an isolcpus flag list the domain and managed_irq flags are lost too; '__setup("nohz_full=", housekeeping_nohz_full_setup);' has no #ifdef; host kallsyms has housekeeping_nohz_full_setup and housekeeping_isolcpus_setup but no rcu_nocb_setup or tick_nohz_full_setup. Two corrections to the wording.
verdicts.correction: (1) nohz_full= on this kernel is both warned about AND reported as unknown: housekeeping_nohz_full_setup returns housekeeping_setup's 0, and init/main.c obsolete_checksetup() only returns true when 'p->setup_func(line + n)' is nonzero, so unknown_bootoption() stores the parameter in envp_init and print_unknown_bootoptions() prints 'Unknown kernel command line parameters "%s", will be passed to user space.' Draft S1's 'reported as unknown parameters and ignored' is therefore right in effect for both nohz_full= and rcu_nocbs=; only S1's reason (no handler) is wrong for nohz_full=. The same return-0 path applies to a misspelled isolcpus flag ('isolcpus: Invalid flag %.*s' then return 0), so the post-reboot dmesg check must also grep 'Invalid flag'. (2) 'only nohz_full can reduce that (to the residual 1 Hz tick plus the task's own timers)': on current kernels the residual 1 Hz tick of a nohz_full CPU is a remote tick run on a housekeeping CPU (kernel/sched/core.c sched_tick_start(): 'if (housekeeping_cpu(cpu, HK_TYPE_KERNEL_NOISE)) return;' then 'queue_delayed_work(system_dfl_wq, &twork->work, HZ);'; cpu-isolation.rst: 'Housekeeping CPUs must run a 1Hz residual remote scheduler tick on behalf of the isolated CPUs.'). A nohz_full pass CPU running one user task with no tick dependency receives zero tick interrupts; what remains on it are its own hrtimers and tick dependencies (POSIX CPU timers, perf sampling, a second runnable task).

verdicts.reason: Mechanism confirmed in source: kernel/rcu/tree_exp.h __sync_rcu_exp_select_node_cpus() takes 'snap = ct_rcu_watching_cpu_acquire(cpu); if (rcu_watching_snap_in_eqs(snap)) mask_ofl_test |= mask;' and IPIs the rest with 'ret = smp_call_function_single(cpu, rcu_exp_handler, NULL, 0);'; fs/namespace.c namespace_unlock() does 'if (likely(hlist_empty(&head))) return; synchronize_rcu_expedited();' (mount teardown). On this kernel user mode is not an extended quiescent state (no CONFIG_CONTEXT_TRACKING_USER, 'context_tracking_enabled' absent from kallsyms), so a busy CPU is IPI'd and an idle one is skipped. Replicated: 4 s spin on CPU 125 with 3x timedatectl that started systemd-timedated (ExecMainStartTimestamp 01:20:16 UTC, PrivateTmp=yes ProtectSystem=strict ProtectHome=yes) -> IPI1=26; control -> 0; idle CPU with the same calls -> 2. Two corrections to the attribution, and one large omission (see extra findings: /sys/kernel/rcu_normal).
verdicts.correction: The IPIs come from the sandboxed service's start (its mount-namespace setup/teardown), not from D-Bus or status queries: with systemd-timedated already running, 3x timedatectl during a 4 s spin gave IPI1=0 (test A), and 3x 'systemctl is-active apt-daily.timer' plus one 'ps -eLo' plus one 'cat /proc/interrupts' gave IPI1=0 (test B). So 'every ssh login' and 'every systemd service start' are not established; the established trigger is any service start or stop that creates or tears down a mount namespace (every sandboxed unit: fwupd-refresh, man-db, systemd-timedated, ...). The service's later idle-exit teardown was not measured. The rate quoted for 23:47-00:42 UTC (2.5 IPI1/s over 8 CPUs) includes the inspections' own service activations. And the implication 'a concrete item that only the rebuilt nohz_full kernel removes' is wrong: writing 1 to /sys/kernel/rcu_normal (root, live, reversible; mode 0644 on the host, current value 0) or booting with rcupdate.rcu_normal=1 makes synchronize_rcu_expedited() fall back to a normal grace period ('if (rcu_gp_is_normal()) { synchronize_rcu_normal(); return; }'), which removes these IPIs on the current kernel.

'cpumask_and(tmp_mask, mask, hk_mask); if (!cpumask_intersects(tmp_mask, cpu_online_mask)) prog_mask = mask;' (requested mask kept when it has no housekeeping CPU). kernel-parameters.txt managed_irq text as quoted ('best effort', 'no effect on the interrupt routing decision', 'only delivered when tasks running on those isolated CPUs submit IO'). blk-mq picks the hardware queue from the submitting CPU, so the one-queue-per-CPU statement holds.
verdicts.correction: The open errno question is settled: kernel/irq/proc.c at tag v7.1 has 'if (!irq_can_set_affinity_usr(irq) || no_irq_affinity) return -EPERM;' (v6.8: 'return -EIO;'), so on the 7.1.3 kernel the safe root test should print 'Operation not permitted'. Precision on 'fires only for I/O submitted from CPU N': page-cache writeback is submitted by the unbound flusher kworker (today 'kworker/u528:0-flush-259:3' sat on CPU 124, earlier on 127), which after isolcpus=domain runs on housekeeping CPUs; only I/O issued synchronously from the pass CPU (direct I/O, fsync-driven writeback, uncached reads) completes on the pass CPU's queue.

Host kallsyms has tmigr_init_isolation, workqueue_unbound_housekeeping_update, kthreads_update_housekeeping, kthread_fetch_affinity. Confidence can be raised from medium to high.

'rcu_assign_pointer(housekeeping.cpumasks[HK_TYPE_DOMAIN], trial);' then 'pci_probe_flush_workqueue(); mem_cgroup_flush_workqueue(); vmstat_flush_workqueue();' 'workqueue_unbound_housekeeping_update(housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN))' 'tmigr_isolated_exclude_cpumask(isol_mask)' 'kthreads_update_housekeeping()'; HK_TYPE_MANAGED_IRQ is not touched. cgroup-v2.rst: 'isolated' = CPUs 'in an isolated state without any load balancing from the scheduler and excluded from the unbound workqueues'; a local partition needs a valid partition-root parent (the root cgroup is one), non-empty exclusive effective CPUs, and cpuset.cpus.exclusive is optional for a local partition (it mirrors cpuset.cpus); an invalid state reads 'isolated invalid (<reason>)'. kernel-parameters.txt domain flag: this isolation 'is irreversible' and cpusets are advised for runtime changes; cpu-isolation.rst: 'cpuset isolated partitions are recommended because they are tunable at runtime.' verdicts.reason: The core semantic is right: arm64 invalidates remote TLBs with broadcast TLBI instructions, not IPIs (no ipi_flush_tlb*/flush_tlb_ipi* symbol in the host kallsyms; absence of a symbol is weak evidence, but it agrees with the architecture). Host MIDR 0x410fd832 = Arm part 0xd83 variant 0 revision 2 = Neoverse V3AE r0p2 (lscpu 'Stepping: r0p2'), which is in the erratum list. The CVE pair (CVE-2026-53354 kernel-side, Arm CVE-2025-10263 hardware) and the fix title 'arm64: errata: Mitigate TLBI errata on various Arm CPUs' are confirmed by Red Hat Bugzilla 2495939 and the CVE trackers; the mitigation is an additional TLBI;DSB after each affected sequence. L3 131072K shared=0-127 is in the evidence.
verdicts.correction: In the current tree the dmesg string belongs to a capability named ARM64_WORKAROUND_REPEAT_TLBI_SYNC: arch/arm64/kernel/cpu_errata.c has '.desc = "Broken broadcast TLBI completion"', '.capability = ARM64_WORKAROUND_REPEAT_TLBI_SYNC', '.match_list = arm64_repeat_tlbi_list', guarded by CONFIG_ARM64_WORKAROUND_REPEAT_TLBI_SYNC; arm64_repeat_tlbi_list's CONFIG_ARM64_ERRATUM_4118414 entry covers Neoverse-V3AE among others. So write 'REPEAT_TLBI_SYNC workaround (erratum 4118414 family)' rather than ARM64_WORKAROUND_REPEAT_TLBI. The sentence 'kernel text patching (module load, BPF) that wakes migration/N on all CPUs' is plausible but unverified: on arm64 multi-instruction patching (ftrace, kprobes, BPF trampolines) goes through aarch64_insn_patch_text() -> stop_machine (both symbols present on the host), while module loading alone does not; label it a hypothesis.

verdicts.reason: The analyst confirmed 'nohz_full reduces it to the residual 1 Hz tick'. On current kernels that residual tick is executed remotely on a housekeeping CPU (sched_tick_remote on system_dfl_wq, queued only for CPUs that are not KERNEL_NOISE housekeeping), so the isolated CPU receives no tick interrupt while a single user task runs without tick dependencies.
verdicts.correction: Phrase D1's limitation as: current kernel = 250 Hz tick on the busy pass CPU; rebuilt nohz_full kernel = zero periodic tick on the pass CPU (1 Hz remote tick on a housekeeping CPU), subject to the single-task and no-POSIX-CPU-timer rules.

extra_findings: E1 (changes P1/P3/P5): the expedited-RCU function-call IPIs (N4) can be removed on the CURRENT kernel without reboot. /sys/kernel/rcu_normal exists on the host with mode -rw-r--r-- root and value 0 (checked 01:10 UTC 22 Oct); kernel/ksysfs.c defines it with KERNEL_ATTR_RW (mode 0644) inside '#ifndef CONFIG_TINY_RCU'; kernel/rcu/tree_exp.h synchronize_rcu_expedited() has '/* If expedited grace periods are prohibited, fall back to normal. */ if (rcu_gp_is_normal()) { synchronize_rcu_normal(); return; }' and kernel/rcu/update.c rcu_gp_is_normal() is 'READ_ONCE(rcu_normal) && rcu_scheduler_active != RCU_SCHEDULER_INIT'. findings.claim: The large interrupt counts on CPUs 122-126 during churn-r1 (1.13 M, 0.89 M, 1.32 M and 0.87 M interrupts in 172.9 s on CPUs 122, 123, 124 and 126, that is 5,000-7,700 per second each; CPU 124's job-time count is 92 % of its since-boot total) cannot be IPIs (125,727 IPIs on 120-127 since boot) and are most likely the job's own hrtimer expiries on the per-CPU arch_timer line (hypothesis): the runtime's event waker ticks every 50 us (up to 20,000 wakeups per second) and the fake device sleeps once per pass. IRQ-affinity settings cannot move a CPU's own timer interrupts, so irqaffinity and managed_irq (draft F10/P2) will not quiet these CPUs; thread placement would.

findings.implication: Do not read isol.py's per-CPU interrupt deltas as host noise; they scale with the job. For the pass core (CPU 127: 40,859 interrupts in 172.9 s = 236 per second, the 250 Hz tick) the host is already quiet. Only nohz_full would remove the tick, and it is not available on this kernel.

Method: every quoted line was looked up in the seven evidence files; claims resting on host-only greps/seds were re-run read-only over ssh on 2026-10-22 about 01:00 UTC (each command under 20 s, nothing written); the three Linux-documentation claims were re-fetched (man7 sudoers(5), man7 PR_SET_TIMERSLACK(2const), kernel/workqueue.c on torvalds master).

verdicts.reason: The key fingerprints, the authorized_keys mtime (16:53 UTC), the sshd settings and drop-in names, the locked password (passwd -S field 'L') and the journal timestamps all exist as quoted. Two attributions go beyond the evidence. (1) 'added from Jibin's workstation' is an inference: authorized_keys was created in the first positron-perf session (the .ssh directory mtime is 05:14 UTC, the session from 192.168.2.136 ended 05:14:12 UTC) and last written at 16:53 UTC, when the only positron-perf sessions were three from 192.168.2.136 ending 16:52:45, 16:53:44 and 16:53:59 UTC; the evidence holds no log of the write itself, and the arm console session on tty1 (open since 20 Oct 19:31 UTC) cannot be excluded. (2) 'Jeremy's first session at 17:07 UTC' names a person the evidence does not identify: the journal shows a positron-perf session from 192.168.1.200 ending 17:07:34 UTC and one from 192.168.2.39 ending 17:07:35 UTC, and 192.168.1.200 ('alpha') also carried the arm administrator's sessions on 20-21 Oct. 'an account with no password' should read 'a locked password'. Action caveat: a drop-in holding 'Match User positron-perf' must end with a 'Match all' line (or be the last file), because sshd's Include splices sshd_config.d files in at the top of sshd_config and a Match block runs until the next Match line; without it 'sshd -t' will reject the later global directives (for example UsePAM, Subsystem) as not allowed within a Match block.
verdicts.correction: Three ed25519 keys are installed with the quoted fingerprints. authorized_keys was created at 05:14 UTC and last written at 16:53 UTC on 21 Oct; the 16:53 write coincides with three positron-perf sessions from 192.168.2.136 (Jibin's workstation address). The first positron-perf sessions from any other address ended 17:07:34 UTC (192.168.1.200) and 17:07:35 UTC (192.168.2.39); who operated them is not in the evidence. The measured lateness includes work, not only wake delay: FakeDevice::retire() (fake_device.cpp 273-284, host sed) first writes the pass's drain rows if still unwritten ('if (hemi.written == retired) write(hemi);'), stores the retirement, pushes the completion, and only then computes 'late = std::max<std::int64_t>(0, clock_.now_ns() - entry.retire_ns)'. In the spin window writes are deferred into retire() unless they belong to the retiring pass (lines 203-209), so late_mean carries the drain-row write and the ring push, executed on the device thread's CPU, which read 1,600,000 kHz in 26 of 28 samples. Hypothesis (unmeasured, est.): if that cost scales with clock, the performance governor cuts 6.25 us by at most 1.6/2.8, to about 3.6 us (est.), still above the 2.50 us band, so P1a alone may not un-void a run; the measurement is device.late_mean_s of a churn re-run after P1a. verdicts.reason: sudoers(5): listpw 'any' means 'at least one matching entry needs NOPASSWD' to list without a password, and 'The default value is any.' The Tag_Spec section says 'By default, if the NOPASSWD tag is applied to any of a user's entries for the current host, the user will be able to run sudo -l without a password'. Host output 'sudo -l: sudo: a password is required' (inspection '=== network_access ===', produced by 'sudo -n -l 2>&1 | head -2', inspect.sh line 115) therefore proves no NOPASSWD entry for positron-perf on this host, unless the 49-byte file itself sets listpw=always (37 bytes, which would leave no room for a rule). No parse error was printed (a syntax error would appear as the first line of 'sudo -n true 2>&1 | head -1'). Caveat that does not change the verdict: 'sudo -n true' -> 'a password is required' alone proves nothing, because sudo authenticates before it reports a missing entry (sudoers.c sudoers_check_common: sudoers_lookup, then 'switch (check_user(ctx, validated, ctx->mode))', then 'If the user was not allowed to run the command we are done'; check.c sets FLAG_NO_USER_INPUT under MODE_NONINTERACTIVE). A password-gated rule such as 'positron-perf ALL=(root) /usr/bin/cpupower *' (45 bytes) would fit and would be unusable because the account's password is locked. The action is valid: sudoers(5) restricts 'sudo -l -U' to root or 'a user with the ability to run any command as either root or the specified user on the current host', which arm (group sudo) is; 'visudo -cf FILE' is the documented syntax check. Timeline matches inspection '=== logins ===': 'arm pts/1 192.168.2.136 Wed Oct 21 05:09:04 2026 - Wed Oct 21 05:13:54 2026' and followup '-r--r----- 1 root root 49 Oct 21 05:12 positron-perf-setup'.
verdicts.source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/sudoers.5.html (listpw: 'The default value is any'; Tag_Spec NOPASSWD and -l; -U restriction); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudo-project/sudo/main/plugins/sudoers/sudoers.c (lookup -> check_user -> denial order); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudo-project/sudo/main/plugins/sudoers/check.c (MODE_NONINTERACTIVE -> FLAG_NO_USER_INPUT); phoenix-crb-inspection.txt '=== network_access ===', '=== logins ==='; phoenix-crb-followup.txt '=== services_detail ===' sudoers.d listing; host dpkg-query sudo 1.9.15p5-3ubuntu5.24.04.4

verdicts.reason: Mechanisms confirmed. H1: cpufreq show_scaling_cur_freq uses arch_freq_get_on_cpu() (arm64 AMU sample taken at the tick and at idle entry, valid for AMU_SAMPLE_EXP_MS = 20 ms) and otherwise prints policy->cur; a thread that sleeps about 1.1 ms and spins 100 us keeps the sample fresh, so the 1,600,000 kHz readings are delivered-frequency measurements, and the performance governor is a live root write to scaling_governor (0644 root, inspection '=== cpufreq ==='). H2: workqueue_init_early() does 'cpumask_copy(wq_unbound_cpumask, cpu_possible_mask);' then 'restrict_unbound_cpumask("HK_TYPE_DOMAIN", housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN));', so isolcpus=domain removes the CPUs from unbound workqueues; per-CPU workqueues (kworker/N:M) and the HZ=250 tick remain (CONFIG_HZ_250=y, '# CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL is not set'). H3: hrtimer_nanosleep() applies 'current->timer_slack_ns' as the expiry range; PR_SET_TIMERSLACK(2const): init's slack is 50,000 ns, inherited by new threads from the creating thread, not applied under real-time policies; on this host /proc/self/timerslack_ns in a positron-perf ssh session reads 50000 and systemd's TimerSlackNSec is unset (host read). H4: comm is truncated at TASK_COMM_LEN 16 bytes (proc_pid_stat(5)), so 'positron-harnes' is 'positron-harness' and unnamed threads inherit it. Two numeric corrections from a re-read of ~/positron/runs/churn-r1/isol.samples.jsonl (34 samples over 168 s, 28 with harness threads): (a) CPUs 120-126 read 1,600,000 kHz in 193 of 196 CPU-samples (3 read 2,800,000) and CPU 127 read 2,800,000 kHz in 26 of 28 samples (2 read 1,600,000), consistent with '26 of 28' only approximately; (b) 'all non-pass harness threads were in state S at every 5 s sample' is wrong in 4 of 134 observations: positron-harnes was R 3 times and positron-scrub R once; positron-pass was R 27 of 28 times on CPU 127 (psr {122: 1, 127: 27}). Migration of the unnamed threads is real but slow: tids 14795 [120,126], 14854 [120,121,126], 14856 [122,125], 14871 [121,122], 14877 [122,125] changed CPU 1-3 times in 13 samples (about 65 s); the others stayed put.
verdicts.correction: Samples: CPUs 120-126 at 1,600,000 kHz in 193 of 196 CPU-samples; CPU 127 at 2,800,000 kHz in 26 of 28; non-pass harness threads were sleeping (S) in 130 of 134 observations, running (R) in 4; five of the unnamed threads moved CPU 1-3 times during the run. The 1.6 GHz readings are AMU measurements (sample age <= 20 ms), not just the governor's request. isolcpus=domain removes unbound workqueues and the vmstat worker from the isolated CPUs but not per-CPU workqueues or the 250 Hz tick.

verdicts.reason: Readability claims confirmed: cpufreq.c 'cpufreq_freq_attr_ro_perm(cpuinfo_cur_freq, 0400)'; cppc_acpi.c define_one_cppc_ro uses '__ATTR(_name, 0444, show_##_name, NULL)' so feedback_ctrs is 0444; kernel/irq/proc.c creates effective_affinity_list with 0444; drivers/base/cpu.c 'DEVICE_ATTR(isolated, 0444 ...)' and nohz_full under '#ifdef CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL'; sysctl docs: dmesg_restrict 0 = unrestricted; on the host /proc/timer_list is -r-------- root, /proc/config.gz -r--r--r--, /boot/config-7.1.3-... -rw-r--r-- (host ls -l), grub.cfg -rw------- (inspection '=== boot_and_kernels ==='). The feedback_ctrs formula is right: delivered perf = reference_perf x delta_del / delta_ref = 50 x delta_del / delta_ref perf units, and 1 unit = nominal_freq / nominal_perf = 2800 / 140 = 20 MHz, so MHz = 2800 x 50 x delta_del / (delta_ref x 140); with the followup numbers (delta ref 3,004,523,060, delta del 8,399,236,187) it gives 2,795.6 MHz (followup: 'delivered perf = 139.8 units -> est. 2796 MHz'). Three corrections. (1) The dmesg grep pattern 'isolcpus|housekeeping|nohz|rcu_nocbs|Unknown kernel command line|cpufreq' misses both positive confirmations on a future kernel: tick-sched.c prints 'NO_HZ: Full dynticks CPUs: %*pbl.' (NO_HZ with an underscore does not match 'nohz' even with -i) and tree_nocb.h prints 'Offload RCU callbacks from CPUs: %*pbl.'; add 'NO_HZ|dynticks|Offload RCU'. On the current kernel it does catch 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported. Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL' (kernel/sched/isolation.c) and 'Unknown kernel command line parameters "...", will be passed to user space.' (init/main.c print_unknown_bootoptions). (2) Reading acpi_cppc/feedback_ctrs of CPU N executes counters_read_on_cpu() -> 'smp_call_function_single(cpu, func, val, 1)' (arm64 AMU), i.e. one function-call IPI onto CPU N per read; fine for the before/after self-check, but it must not be polled on the pass core during a counted run. (3) 'zcat /proc/config.gz' depends on CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC in the rebuilt kernel; fall back to 'grep -E "CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL|CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU" /boot/config-$(uname -r)' (0644). Also note the self-check's 'cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated' reports only boot-time isolcpus (HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT), never a cpuset partition.

extra_findings: E1 (changes P1c/D2): /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated reports only the boot-time isolcpus mask. drivers/base/cpu.c print_cpus_isolated(): 'cpumask_andnot(isolated, cpu_possible_mask, housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT))', and include/linux/sched/isolation.h documents HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT as 'Inverse of boot-time isolcpus= argument' while HK_TYPE_DOMAIN is the subset that 'also accounts for cpuset isolated partitions'. kernel/sched/isolation.c housekeeping_update() (called for cpuset isolated partitions) rewrites HK_TYPE_DOMAIN at runtime and propagates it to unbound workqueues (workqueue_unbound_housekeeping_update), the timer migration hierarchy (tmigr_isolated_exclude_cpumask) and kthreads (kthreads_update_housekeeping), but never the sysfs 'isolated' file. So the no-reboot cpuset path (draft S4/P1c) would give real kernel-side isolation on a 7.1-class kernel yet churn.py would still record core_isolated=false, isolated_cpus=[]; only the isolcpus reboot flips the recorded field. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/drivers/base/cpu.c, .../include/linux/sched/isolation.h, .../kernel/sched/isolation.c. Version caveat: the DOMAIN_BOOT split is recent; on an older base the file read HK_TYPE_DOMAIN, which was boot-only anyway, so the conclusion holds either way.

E2 (changes the X12 self-check and the P2 verification): on this kernel 'nohz_full=' IS a registered boot parameter (kernel/sched/isolation.c is built under CONFIG_CPU_ISOLATION=y and registers '__setup("nohz_full=", housekeeping_nohz_full_setup)'); housekeeping_setup() prints 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported. Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL' and returns 0, and init/main.c obsolete_checksetup() treats a 0 return as unhandled, so the parameter is also listed in 'Unknown kernel command line parameters "...", will be passed to user space.' and lands in init's environment. 'rcu_nocbs' is registered only under '#ifdef CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU' as '__setup("rcu_nocbs", rcu_nocb_setup)' (no '=' in the registration), so on this kernel it is simply unknown. The form 'isolcpus=nohz,domain,...' makes housekeeping_setup() drop the whole isolcpus setting (same pr_warn, return 0). Positive confirmations on a NO_HZ_FULL kernel are 'NO_HZ: Full dynticks CPUs: %*pbl.' (kernel/time/tick-sched.c) and 'Offload RCU callbacks from CPUs: %*pbl.' (kernel/rcu/tree_nocb.h); neither matches grep -i 'nohz|rcu_nocbs'. Sources: the four raw.githubusercontent.com files named.

E3 (changes P3 clock evidence and any in-run sampler): on arm64 the CPPC feedback counters are AMU registers read on the target CPU: arch/arm64/kernel/topology.c counters_read_on_cpu() -> 'return smp_call_function_single(cpu, func, val, 1);', so each read of /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuN/acpi_cppc/feedback_ctrs (world-readable, 0444) or of root's cpuinfo_cur_freq sends one function-call IPI (IPI1) onto CPU N and wakes it if idle. scaling_cur_freq does not: cpufreq.c show_scaling_cur_freq() prints arch_freq_get_on_cpu() when the per-CPU AMU sample is younger than AMU_SAMPLE_EXP_MS = 20 ms and otherwise falls back to policy->cur, the governor's last request; with one CPU per policy there is no sibling to borrow from (-EAGAIN, seen as 'Resource temporarily unavailable' on cpuinfo_avg_freq). Consequences: sample feedback_ctrs only before and after a counted run; on a future nohz_full kernel the pass core's scaling_cur_freq is a request, not a measurement (full-dynticks CPUs are skipped), so the hand-off should define 'fixed clock' by feedback_ctrs deltas; Jeremy's isol.py cur_khz readings on busy or recently idle CPUs (sample age <= 20 ms) are measurements, which supports H1 as measured, not inferred. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/arch/arm64/kernel/topology.c, .../drivers/cpufreq/cpufreq.c, .../drivers/acpi/cppc_acpi.c; phoenix-crb-followup.txt '=== cpufreq_extra ==='.

E4 (settles H3 as SDK-side): the inherited timer slack on this host is the kernel default. In a positron-perf ssh session /proc/self/timerslack_ns reads 50000 (ns) and /etc/systemd/system.conf and user.conf leave TimerSlackNSec commented (host read); PR_SET_TIMERSLACK(2const): the slack 'is inherited by a child created via fork(2), and is preserved across execve(2)' and new threads copy 'the current value of the creating thread'; hrtimer_nanosleep() arms the sleep with 'hrtimer_set_expires_range_ns(&t.timer, rqtp, current->timer_slack_ns)'. A thread lowers its own slack with prctl(PR_SET_TIMERSLACK, 1000) without any privilege, as runtime/events/waker.cpp already does; no host setting is involved. Sources: host /proc/self/timerslack_ns; https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_TIMERSLACK.2const.html; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/kernel/time/hrtimer.c.

E5 (bounds the P2 IRQ work): /proc/irq/N/smp_affinity is created read-only (no S_IWUSR) and a write returns EPERM when the IRQ is per-CPU, NO_BALANCING or managed (kernel/irq/proc.c write_irq_affinity: 'if (!irq_can_set_affinity_usr(irq) || no_irq_affinity) return -EPERM;'; manage.c irq_can_set_affinity_usr adds '!irqd_affinity_is_managed'). On the host /proc/irq/12/smp_affinity (arch_timer PPI) and /proc/irq/304/smp_affinity (managed nvme0q119) are -r--r--r--. kernel-parameters.txt: irqaffinity= only sets 'the default irq affinity mask'; isolcpus managed_irq is 'best effort' and a queue whose mask holds only isolated CPUs still fires there, 'only delivered when tasks running on those isolated CPUs submit IO'. So the admin cannot move the timer PPI or the NVMe queue IRQs by hand, and the churn label's three 86 MB record writes issued from CPUs 120-126 will keep landing on those CPUs' own nvme queues. Sources: the raw.githubusercontent.com kernel/irq files and kernel-parameters.txt; host ls -l.

E6 (refines X8 H2): isolcpus=domain also stops the per-CPU vmstat worker on the isolated CPUs: mm/vmstat.c vmstat_shepherd() has 'if (cpu_is_isolated(cpu)) continue;' before 'queue_delayed_work_on(cpu, mm_percpu_wq, dw, 0)', and cpu_is_isolated() is '!housekeeping_test_cpu(cpu, HK_TYPE_DOMAIN)'; HK_TYPE_KTHREAD aliases HK_TYPE_DOMAIN, so unbound kthreads are kept off too. What stays: per-CPU workqueue items queued from the isolated CPU itself (kworker/N:M, kblockd), the 250 Hz tick while a task runs, and timers armed by the threads running there (E14). Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/mm/vmstat.c, .../include/linux/sched/isolation.h.

E7 (sharpens X2's proof): sudo authenticates before it decides whether the user is allowed: plugins/sudoers/sudoers.c sudoers_check_common() runs 'validated = sudoers_lookup(...)', then 'switch (check_user(ctx, validated, ctx->mode))', and only afterwards 'If the user was not allowed to run the command we are done'; check.c sets FLAG_NO_USER_INPUT under MODE_NONINTERACTIVE. So 'sudo -n true' -> 'a password is required' is printed for a user with no entry as well; the evidence that positron-perf has no NOPASSWD rule is 'sudo -n -l' plus listpw's default 'any' (sudoers(5): 'The default value is any'). Only the admin can tell whether the 49-byte file is a Defaults line, a rule for another user, or a password-gated rule (unusable: the password is locked). Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudo-project/sudo/main/plugins/sudoers/sudoers.c and check.c; https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/sudoers.5.html.

E8 (bounds the limits.d action in X3): pam_limits is applied by /etc/pam.d/sshd line 40 'session required pam_limits.so' (host read), so a limits.d change reaches every new ssh session and the nohup jobs started from it, but not processes started through the user manager (user@1001.service, 'systemd-run --user'), which take systemd's DefaultLimit* values. If SCHED_FIFO is ever granted: kernel.sched_rt_runtime_us = 950000 (host) reserves 5 % of each 1,000,000 us period for non-real-time tasks (sched(7): default 950,000; -1 'makes the run time the same as the period'), which on older kernels throttled a spinning FIFO thread for 50 ms per second; on 7.1-class kernels with '# CONFIG_RT_GROUP_SCHED is not set' the fair deadline server replaces that throttling and only runs when fair tasks are runnable on the same CPU. Sources: host grep of /etc/pam.d/sshd; https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/sched.7.html; phoenix-crb-inspection.txt '=== sysctl_limits ===', '=== kernel_config ==='.

E9 (sshd hardening scope): Ubuntu 24.04's OpenSSH 1:9.6p1-3ubuntu13.20 confines a Match block in an included file to that file (servconf.c: 'Don't let included files clobber the containing file's Match state', 'oactive = *activep' ... '*activep = oactive'), so a Match drop-in is safe, and sshd uses 'the first obtained value' for global keywords. On this host 'PasswordAuthentication yes' is set in /etc/ssh/sshd_config line 66 and in all three drop-ins (01-arm-svk-password-auth.conf, 60-cloudimg-settings.conf, 99-arm-svk.conf, each 27 or 47 bytes, host read), and 'PermitRootLogin yes' in sshd_config line 42 and 99-arm-svk.conf; a host-wide change would need a drop-in that sorts before 01- (for example 00-positron.conf) and the admin's agreement, since the arm-svk installer wrote those files. The Include is at sshd_config line 12 and 'UsePAM yes' at line 94. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openssh/openssh-portable/V_9_6_P1/servconf.c; https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/sshd_config.5.html; host grep of sshd_config and cat of the drop-ins.

E10 (answers how G6 can be closed): the journal split (journald.conf(5) SplitMode=uid, the default) puts messages from the post-auth sshd process (uid 1001) into positron-perf's own journal and the monitor's 'Accepted publickey for positron-perf from ADDR port N ssh2: ED25519 SHA256:...' line into the system journal; as positron-perf 'journalctl | grep -c Accepted' prints 0 (host). E12 (hrtimer placement, supports X9 and D3): with kernel.timer_migration = 1 (host sysctl) and no nohz_full, hrtimer get_target_base() asks get_nohz_timer_target(), which returns the current CPU whenever it is a HK_TYPE_KERNEL_NOISE housekeeping CPU (every CPU on this kernel) and not idle; a running thread arming nanosleep/futex timers is never idle at that moment, so its timers expire on the CPU it runs on. After isolcpus=domain the scheduler stops balancing threads among 120-126 (kernel-parameters.txt: 'domain: Isolate from the general SMP balancing and scheduling algorithms'), so the per-CPU arch_timer counts and the waker's 20,000 wakeups per second will concentrate on whichever CPUs the unpinned threads first land on; pinning each thread (D3) is what makes the per-CPU interrupt picture reproducible. Corrections: (1) 'ev3-churn-job.sh unchanged' is inconsistent with isolating 126-127: with taskset -c 120-127 and pass core 127, placement() gives the other threads the mask 120-126 (Jeremy's samples record allowed '120-126' for every non-pass thread in all 34 samples), which includes isolated CPU 126; a thread first placed on 126 is then never balanced away. Six corrections from `systemctl cat`/`show` on the host (22 Oct 01:07 UTC): (1) fwupd-refresh.timer is HOURLY and missing from the finding: 'OnCalendar=*-*-* *:00:00 / RandomizedDelaySec=1h / Persistent=true', service 'ExecStart=/usr/bin/fwupdmgr refresh' (last Thu 00:08:44 UTC, next 01:28:26 UTC) - it fires inside every run window. (2) motd-news.timer 'OnCalendar=00,12:00:00 / RandomizedDelaySec=12h / Persistent=true / OnStartupSec=1min' (next Thu 23:47:27 UTC): the 12:00 slot can land anywhere 12:00-24:00 UTC, i.e. inside 13:00-21:00; runs '/etc/update-motd.d/50-motd-news --force'. (3) update-notifier-download.timer is boot-relative, 'OnStartupSec=5m / OnUnitActiveSec=24h', Persistent=no; systemd-tmpfiles-clean.timer is also monotonic ('NextElapseUSecMonotonic=2d 15min', Persistent=no). 'About 19:11 / 19:21 UTC' holds only for the current boot; after a Thu 15:00 UTC reboot they fire at about 15:05 and 15:15 UTC and then daily at those times, inside the window and inside Jeremy's morning. (4) sysstat: '/etc/default/sysstat' has ENABLED="false", so the cron.d debian-sa1 lines are no-ops; only sysstat-collect.service ('ExecStart=/usr/lib/sysstat/sa1 1 1', every 10 min) could collect (whether it writes /var/log/sysstat is unchecked). (5) unattended-upgrades.service is 'ExecStart=/usr/share/unattended-upgrades/unattended-upgrade-shutdown --wait-for-signal', a shutdown hook; installs are run by apt-daily-upgrade.service 'ExecStart=/usr/lib/apt/apt.systemd.daily install'. Disabling the two apt timers is the lever; disabling the service is harmless but not what stops kernel installs. (6) netperf: the process is '1861 root psr=32 netserver'; the generated unit reports 'MainPID=0 ... SubState=running' with KillMode=process, so `systemctl stop` relies entirely on '/etc/init.d/netperf stop'; verify with `pgrep -a netserver` afterwards. Also: Persistent=true on apt-daily, apt-daily-upgrade, fstrim, fwupd-refresh, motd-news, man-db means re-enabling after 6 Nov triggers an immediate catch-up run (systemd.timer: the service runs right away if it would have fired while the timer was off; 'Catch-up runs still respect RandomizedDelaySec=').

'The boot CPU will be forced outside the range to maintain the timekeeping.' 'Any CPUs in this list will have their RCU callbacks offloaded, just as if they had also been called out in the rcu_nocbs= boot parameter.'; rcu_nocbs: 'In kernels built with CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU=y, enable the no-callback CPU mode'. verdicts.reason: Confirmed semantics: isolcpus= 'Format: [flag-list,]<cpu-list>'; domain 'Isolate from the general SMP balancing and scheduling algorithms.'; 'Note that performing domain isolation this way is irreversible'; managed_irq 'Isolate from being targeted by managed interrupts which have an interrupt mask containing isolated CPUs.' and 'If a queue's affinity mask contains only isolated CPUs then this parameter has no effect on the interrupt routing decision' (so the one-queue-per-CPU NVMe IRQs on 126/127 stay there and fire only for IO submitted from 126/127); irqaffinity= '[SMP] Set the default irq affinity mask' (kernel/irq/irqdesc.c also forces the boot CPU into it); cpufreq.default_governor= 'must be registered in the kernel before the cpufreq driver probes' (drivers/cpufreq/cpufreq.c `module_param_string(default_governor, ...)`, cpufreq_init_policy: `if (policy->last_governor[0] != '\0') gov = get_governor(policy->last_governor); else gov = get_governor(default_governor);`; CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_GOV_PERFORMANCE=y is built in, cppc_cpufreq=m probes later). The no-balancing premise is confirmed and its mechanism is sharper than stated: a new thread starts on its creator's CPU (kernel/sched/core.c sched_cgroup_fork: `__set_task_cpu(p, smp_processor_id());`, wake_up_new_task: `__set_task_cpu(p, select_task_rq(p, task_cpu(p), &wake_flags));` with WF_FORK); select_task_rq_fair runs `for_each_domain(cpu, tmp)` on the waking CPU, finds no domain on an isolated CPU, and returns `new_cpu = prev_cpu` for fork/exec; for wakeups select_idle_sibling() ends with `sd = rcu_dereference_all(per_cpu(sd_llc, target)); if (!sd) return target;` - a thread on an isolated CPU always returns to it. A thread migrates only when its new affinity mask excludes its current CPU (core.c: 'Can the task run on the task's current CPU? If so, we're done'), and then to `cpumask_any_and_distribute(cpu_valid_mask, ctx->new_mask)`, which rotates through the mask. REFUTED part: 'leave Jeremy's ev3-churn-job.sh unchanged (taskset 120-127 ... others on 120-126 where 120-125 stay kernel-balanced)'. (1) With 126 isolated and inside churn.py's run_cpus (job minus pass core = 120-126), any thread placed on 126 is stuck there for the whole run. (2) `taskset -c 120-127 prlimit ... bash ...` is executed from a CPU outside the mask, so taskset's sched_setaffinity moves the chain to a rotating CPU of 120-127, which can be 126 or 127 (2 of 8); every fork/exec from an isolated CPU stays on it, so bash, python (churn.py client and latency judge) and the harness's non-pass threads would all sit on 126, or on 127 beside the pass thread, with nothing to move them. The same 1-in-8 trap exists with 127 alone. Expected post-reboot values the finding omits: /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask = 3fffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff and cpumask_isolated = c0000000,00000000,00000000,00000000 (kernel/workqueue.c workqueue_init_early: `restrict_unbound_cpumask("HK_TYPE_DOMAIN", housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN));` and `cpumask_andnot(wq_isolated_cpumask, cpu_possible_mask, housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN));`); /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated = 126-127 (HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT); default_smp_affinity = 00ffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff. The optional live write of 0-119 to the workqueue cpumask is valid (`DEVICE_ATTR_RW(cpumask)`; workqueue_set_unbound_cpumask intersects with cpu_possible_mask and rejects an empty result).
verdicts.correction: Keep isolcpus=domain,managed_irq,126-127 irqaffinity=0-119 cpufreq.default_governor=performance, but the job must change: (a) the job mask must not contain an isolated CPU other than the pass core, so churn.py's run_cpus is 120-125 and its 'last CPU' pass core is 127: use mask 120-125,127; (b) the launcher chain must start on a non-isolated CPU: `taskset -c 120-125 taskset -c 120-125,127 prlimit ... bash tools/ci/run_scheduled_gate.sh churn ...` (the outer call lands the chain on 120-125; the inner widening does not migrate because the current CPU is in the new mask). CPU 126 stays idle, reserved for a future pinned fake-device thread. Equivalent minimal variant: isolate 127 only with `taskset -c 120-126 taskset -c 120-127 ...`. Acceptance in isol.samples.jsonl: no thread with psr=126 (two-core variant) and no non-pass thread with psr=127. Add the expected workqueue cpumask (3fffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff) to the post-reboot checks. Note the managed_irq flag does nothing for the per-CPU NVMe queues on 126/127.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed: under the performance governor the sysfs request is constant - cpufreq.rst: performance 'causes the highest frequency, within the scaling_max_freq policy limit, to be requested for that policy'; scaling_cur_freq 'Usually this reflects the last P-state the driver requested rather than the actual hardware frequency'; drivers/cpufreq/cpufreq.c show_scaling_cur_freq uses arch_freq_get_on_cpu only when `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CPUFREQ_ARCH_CUR_FREQ)`, which is absent from the host's /proc/config.gz, so the file returns policy->cur; cppc_cpufreq never sets policy->freq_table (`__resolve_freq`: `if (!policy->freq_table) return target_freq;`), which is why schedutil samples show continuous values such as 1758203 kHz, and why 2800000 appears exactly under a max request (Jeremy's freq.spin.txt '75 2800000'). The delivered-clock formula is the kernel's own: drivers/cpufreq/cppc_cpufreq.c cppc_perf_from_fbctrs `return (reference_perf * delta_delivered) / delta_reference;`. Three corrections: (1) MEASURED on the host: every read of /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuN/acpi_cppc/feedback_ctrs sends two function-call IPIs to CPU N ('IPI1 delta after 10 feedback_ctrs reads of cpu121: 20'; 'after 10 scaling_cur_freq reads: 0'; '1 s idle control: 1'), because arch/arm64/kernel/topology.c counters_read_on_cpu() reads the AMU counters with `smp_call_function_single(cpu, func, val, 1);`. So the clock rule must be one before/after pair of reads on the pass core per run, never periodic polling of CPU 127 during a counted run; isol.py's 5 s sampler must keep reading scaling_cur_freq (no IPI); root's cpuinfo_cur_freq costs 4 IPIs per read (cppc_cpufreq_get_rate samples twice with `udelay(2)`). (2) Whether the counters advance during WFI is not documented in topology.c (no such comment), so the rule should say 'delivered-perf ratio from one before/after pair', not 'over the whole run' in wall-clock terms. (3) cpuinfo_avg_freq's EAGAIN on an idle CPU is expected (arch_freq_get_on_cpu: 'No alternative to pull info from' -> -EAGAIN for a one-CPU policy). Window defaults also need the SO2 corrections (hourly fwupd-refresh; boot-relative timers inside the window after the reboot) and the SO1 DST fix (06:00 UTC for Jeremy).
verdicts.correction: Clock rule: (a) all 128 scaling_governor = performance; (b) scaling_cur_freq = 2800000 on policies 120-127 in every isol.py sample (this is the requested frequency, no IPI cost); (c) delivered clock from exactly one feedback_ctrs read before and one after the run on the pass CPU: reference_perf x delta_delivered / delta_reference >= 138.6 perf units (= 2772 MHz, 99 % of 2800 MHz); never poll feedback_ctrs or cpuinfo_cur_freq of the pass core during a counted run (2 and 4 IPIs per read). Window: 13:00-21:00 UTC Mon-Fri only after fwupd-refresh, motd-news, update-notifier-download and systemd-tmpfiles-clean are disabled (SO2). DST line: Jeremy's offset changes at 06:00 UTC on 1 Nov.

extra_findings: Launcher trap on isolated CPUs (changes P2, P5, SO8, SO11-Q3, SO12): `taskset -c <mask> cmd` executed from a CPU outside <mask> migrates the process to `cpumask_any_and_distribute(cpu_valid_mask, new_mask)` (kernel/sched/core.c __set_cpus_allowed_ptr_locked; lib/cpumask.c rotates per CPU), which can be an isolated CPU; from an isolated CPU every fork and exec stays on that CPU (sched_cgroup_fork `__set_task_cpu(p, smp_processor_id())`; select_task_rq_fair finds no sched domain and returns prev_cpu; sched_exec returns early when dest == current CPU) and wakeups return to it (select_idle_sibling: `if (!sd) return target;`). With Jeremy's `taskset -c 120-127 ...` and isolcpus on 126-127 the whole bash/python chain lands on 126 or 127 in 2 of 8 launches and never leaves. Fix: `taskset -c 120-125 taskset -c 120-125,127 ...` (land on a balanced CPU first; widening the mask does not migrate because 'Can the task run on the task's current CPU? If so, we're done'). Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/kernel/sched/core.c, .../kernel/sched/fair.c, .../lib/cpumask.c; phoenix-crb-round3.txt section runs_and_checks (ev3-churn-job.sh).

Reading /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuN/acpi_cppc/feedback_ctrs costs two function-call IPIs on CPU N (measured on the host 2026-10-22 01:07 UTC: 10 reads of cpu121 -> IPI1 +20; 10 scaling_cur_freq reads -> +0; 1 s idle control -> +1), because arch/arm64/kernel/topology.c counters_read_on_cpu() uses `smp_call_function_single(cpu, func, val, 1)` for the AMU counters; cpuinfo_cur_freq (root) costs 4 (cppc_cpufreq_get_rate samples twice with udelay(2)). Any clock monitoring of the pass core during a counted run must be limited to scaling_cur_freq (no IPI) plus one feedback_ctrs pair before/after. Sources: host command result; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/arch/arm64/kernel/topology.c; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/drivers/cpufreq/cppc_cpufreq.c.

Persistent=true (apt-daily, apt-daily-upgrade, fstrim, fwupd-refresh, motd-news, man-db; stamp files under /var/lib/systemd/timers/) means re-enabling a timer after the demo triggers an immediate catch-up run, delayed only by RandomizedDelaySec (systemd.timer(5): the service runs right away if it would have fired while the timer was off; 'Catch-up runs still respect RandomizedDelaySec='). nohz_full= is a registered parameter even on this kernel: kernel/sched/isolation.c has `__setup("nohz_full=", housekeeping_nohz_full_setup);` with no #ifdef, and housekeeping_setup() prints 'Housekeeping: nohz unsupported. Build with CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL' and ignores the setting; rcu_nocbs= is unregistered (kernel/rcu/tree_nocb.h `__setup("rcu_nocbs", rcu_nocb_setup);` inside `#ifdef CONFIG_RCU_NOCB_CPU`) and would be listed by init/main.c as 'Unknown kernel command line parameters "...", will be passed to user space.' Draft S1's 'both reported as unknown parameters' is therefore half right. On a NO_HZ_FULL rebuild, nohz_full= and isolcpus= must carry identical CPU lists ('Housekeeping: nohz_full= must match isolcpus='), managed_irq excepted. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/kernel/sched/isolation.c, .../kernel/rcu/tree_nocb.h, .../init/main.c.

With isolcpus=domain the kernel moves init to the housekeeping CPUs (kernel/sched/core.c sched_init_smp: '/* Move init over to a non-isolated CPU */' `if (set_cpus_allowed_ptr(current, housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN)) < 0) BUG();`), so after the reboot every service, timer job and ssh session inherits a mask without 126-127; CPUs 120-125 stay open to all of them. Optional complement at the same reboot: `CPUAffinity=0-119` in /etc/systemd/system.conf (systemd-system.conf(5): 'the CPU affinity for the service manager as well as the default CPU affinity for all forked off processes'; per-unit overrides allowed) keeps system services off 120-127 entirely; user jobs still reach 120-127 through taskset/sched_setaffinity ('You can move a process onto or off an "isolated" CPU via the CPU affinity syscalls or cpuset'). Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/kernel/sched/core.c; https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-system.conf.html; kernel-parameters.txt isolcpus=.

The running kernel is of the dynamic-housekeeping generation: `ls /sys/devices/system/cpu/` on the host shows a 'housekeeping' attribute next to 'isolated' (not present in older kernels). In this generation (torvalds/master as fetched) /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated lists only boot-time isolcpus CPUs (drivers/base/cpu.c: `cpumask_andnot(isolated, cpu_possible_mask, housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN_BOOT))`), while a cgroup-v2 cpuset isolated partition calls housekeeping_update() (kernel/cgroup/cpuset.c cpuset_update_sd_hk_unlock: `WARN_ON_ONCE(housekeeping_update(isolated_hk_cpus));`), which updates HK_TYPE_DOMAIN, unbound workqueues (workqueue_unbound_housekeeping_update), timer migration (tmigr_isolated_exclude_cpumask) and kthread affinity (kthreads_update_housekeeping). Consequence for draft P1c (no-reboot cpuset path): it now covers scheduler domains, unbound workqueues, timer migration and kthreads, but not managed-IRQ steering, not nohz_full, and not the sysfs 'isolated' marker that churn.py's core_isolated reads (it would stay false). Caveat: the vendor 7.1.3 tree is inferred from the sysfs attribute, not read; a root test is `echo isolated > <cgroup>/cpuset.cpus.partition` then `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset.cpus.isolated` and `cat /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask_isolated`. Sources: host `ls /sys/devices/system/cpu/`; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/drivers/base/cpu.c, .../kernel/sched/isolation.c, .../kernel/cgroup/cpuset.c, .../kernel/workqueue.c.

Expected sysfs values after the planned reboot (missing from the checklists): /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated = '126-127'; /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask = '3fffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff' (workqueue_init_early: `restrict_unbound_cpumask("HK_TYPE_DOMAIN", housekeeping_cpumask(HK_TYPE_DOMAIN))`); /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask_isolated = 'c0000000,00000000,00000000,00000000'; /proc/irq/default_smp_affinity = '00ffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff,ffffffff' (irqaffinity=0-119; kernel/irq/irqdesc.c irq_affinity_setup also forces the boot CPU in). Today all three workqueue masks read ffffffff,... / ffffffff,... / 00000000,... (host check). Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/kernel/workqueue.c; .../kernel/irq/irqdesc.c; host check 2026-10-22 01:07 UTC.

scaling_cur_freq on this kernel reports the last REQUEST (policy->cur), not the delivered clock: drivers/cpufreq/cpufreq.c show_scaling_cur_freq consults arch_freq_get_on_cpu only under `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CPUFREQ_ARCH_CUR_FREQ)`, absent from /proc/config.gz; cppc_cpufreq has no freq_table (`if (!policy->freq_table) return target_freq;`), hence continuous schedutil values such as 1758203 kHz and exact 2800000 under a max request; cpufreq.rst: 'Usually this reflects the last P-state the driver requested rather than the actual hardware frequency'. cpuinfo_avg_freq is the AMU-derived average and returns EAGAIN on an idle one-CPU policy (arch_freq_get_on_cpu: 'No alternative to pull info from'). Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/drivers/cpufreq/cpufreq.c, .../drivers/cpufreq/cppc_cpufreq.c, .../arch/arm64/kernel/topology.c, .../Documentation/admin-guide/pm/cpufreq.rst; host `zcat /proc/config.gz | grep CPUFREQ_ARCH_CUR_FREQ` (no match).

managed_irq is a no-op for the per-CPU NVMe queues on 126/127: kernel-parameters.txt isolcpus= 'If a queue's affinity mask contains only isolated CPUs then this parameter has no effect on the interrupt routing decision', and kernel/irq/manage.c irq_do_set_affinity keeps the requested mask when it does not intersect the housekeeping mask (isolated targets 'only receiving interrupts when the I/O operation was submitted' from them). So the pass thread must not write files from 127, or its own NVMe completions (nvme0q126/nvme1q126, effective affinity 127) land on the pass core. Sources: kernel-parameters.txt; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/kernel/irq/manage.c; phoenix-crb-inspection.txt section interrupts.

grub-reboot is one-shot only when GRUB can write grubenv: grub-reboot(8) 'In cases where GRUB cannot write to the environment block, such as when it is stored on an MDRAID or LVM device, the chosen boot menu entry will remain the default even after reboot.' Here /boot is a plain ext4 partition (/dev/nvme0n1p16, inspection storage), so the vendor entry returns on the following boot as SO14 expects; a rebuilt kernel must use a distinct version string so that its package does not overwrite the vendor files. Sources: https://manpages.debian.org/bookworm/grub2-common/grub-reboot.8.en.html; phoenix-crb-inspection.txt sections storage and boot_and_kernels.
